#912. Vote for the first BBC Men's Footballer of the Year

Voting is now open for the BBC Men's Footballer of the Year 2026 award, which will be presented at Sports Personality of the Year.

Fans from the UK can vote from the five-player shortlist of Jude Bellingham, Harry Kane, Kylian Mbappe, Rodri and Lamine Yamal.

The vote closes on Friday, 27 November at 09:00 GMT.

The winner of the award - new for this year - will be presented during the live Sports Personality of the Year show on Sunday, 13 December.

Alex Kay-Jelski, Director of BBC Sport, said: "From the drama and excitement of the men's World Cup to the moments that have captivated fans across the domestic and international game, 2026 has given us so much to celebrate.

"Our inaugural BBC Men's Footballer of the Year award is about recognising the players who have made this year so special, inspired fans and left their mark on the game.

"It's a fantastic shortlist, and I can't wait to see who the public choose as our first-ever winner."

The shortlist was selected by an expert panel comprising former international players and some of the BBC's most respected football voices, bringing together a wealth of experience and insight from across the game.

The panel included Cesar Azpilicueta (Spain), Scott Brown (Scotland), Olivier Giroud (France), Shay Given (Republic of Ireland), Hassan Kachloul (Morocco), Lucas Leiva (Brazil), Benni McCarthy (South Africa), Alan Shearer, Ellen White (both England) and Ashley Williams (Wales).

Read more on the five contenders and cast your vote below.

Sorry, this vote cannot be loaded. In order to vote you need to enable JavaScript in your browser.

Meet the SPOTY Men's Footballer of the Year contenders

Bellingham made history this summer as he became the first Englishman to score as many as seven goals at a major tournament.

In a superb World Cup for the midfielder, he memorably netted twice in back-to-back games to help the Three Lions beat Mexico and Norway.

That meant he joined exalted company as the first player to score two or more goals in successive World Cup knockout games since Diego Maradona in 1986, and the second youngest in history behind Pele in 1958.

Bellingham also became the youngest European player to make an appearance at four different major tournaments, and also reached the milestone of 50 caps at a younger age than any other England men's player.

The goals continued to flow for Real Madrid, too, with Bellingham notching his 50th for the club to move above the legendary Zinedine Zidane in the Los Blancos' all-time scoring charts.

Bellingham was recently joined in the England squad by his brother Jobe

In a stunning year of goalscoring, Kane become the first Englishman for 25 years (and only fifth in history) to win the Ballon d'Or - awarded to the world's best footballer.

His tally of 73 goals in 65 matches for club and country during a stellar 2025-26 season has only been surpassed in one of Europe's top five leagues by Lionel Messi's 82 for Barcelona and Argentina in 2011-12.

Kane scored 61 of those goals in just 51 appearances for Bayern Munich as he helped the Bavarians to a league and cup double. His total was 19 more than any other player in Europe's top five divisions.

Already England's record goalscorer, he surpassed Peter Shilton's mark of 125 appearances to become the most-capped Englishman in history.

Six goals at this summer's World Cup also helped him overtake Gary Lineker as the Three Lions' record scorer at the tournament, while he joined David Beckham as the only Englishmen to score in three separate World Cups.

Kane scored his first England goal 79 seconds into his debut in 2015

Mbappe came out on top of an enthralling tussle with Lionel Messi at the 2026 World Cup to become the leading goalscorer in the tournament's history.

The France forward, who is still only 27, took his tally to 22 from just three World Cups to finish one ahead of the great Argentine.

Mbappe's 10 goals from eight games this summer meant he won his second World Cup Golden Boot - a feat no player has managed before.

It also made him the first man to reach double figures at a World Cup since Gerd Muller in 1970, with only Just Fontaine (13) and Sandor Kocsis (11) having scored more goals in a single tournament.

Other achievements in a standout year included him finishing runner-up in the Ballon d'Or awards and overtaking Olivier Giroud as France's all-time leading goalscorer.

He scored 25 times to retain his title as La Liga's top scorer during a 2025-26 campaign in which he netted 42 goals in all competitions for Real Madrid.

Mbappe has won eight consecutive league golden boots

Midfield maestro Rodri earned yet another accolade in his incredible career when he was awarded the Golden Ball trophy for the World Cup's best player.

By captaining Spain to glory in the US, Rodri became only the fourth male player to win the World Cup, European Championship, Champions League and Ballon d'Or - following in the footsteps of legendary Germans Gerd Muller and Franz Beckenbauer and France's Zinedine Zidane.

His achievements were made all the more special given doubts remained over whether he would recapture his best form after a long recovery from a serious knee injury in 2024.

Then Manchester City boss Pep Guardiola predicted he would return to his best at the World Cup and he was right. Rodri completed 756 passes there - the most in the tournament since records began in 1966.

His final season at Manchester City before departing for Barcelona ended in familiar fashion with a domestic cup double taking his trophy haul with the club to 14.

Rodri scored the goal that won Manchester City the Champions League in 2023

Lamine Yamal continues to rewrite the record books with his astonishing exploits for club and country.

Just days after his 19th birthday, the Spaniard became the youngest footballer to have played in - and won - both a World Cup and a European Championship. The only players younger than him to play in a World Cup final are Brazil's Pele in 1958 and Giuseppe Bergomi for Italy in 1982.

For the second year running, his performances led to a podium place at the Ballon d'Or and at the same award ceremony he became the first footballer in history to win the Young Talent of the Year three years in succession.

At club level, he was named La Liga's Best Player courtesy of a starring role in Barcelona's title success. The teenager ended the season with an impressive 24 goals and 18 assists across all competitions.

He recently broke Kylian Mbappe's record for the most goals by a teenager in Champions League history.

Lamine Yamal was 16 years and 362 days when he scored at the European Championship in 2024

#911. 'We feel the pain': Pochettino on 4-0 defeat at Liverpool to start Manchester United era – video

Liverpool thrashed 10-man Manchester United 4-0 at Anfield on Sunday to climb to fourth in the Premier League. But the defeat left United 19th, only one point above bottom-placed Crystal Palace. There was no new manager bounce for Mauricio Pochettino, who saw Leny Yoro sent off in the eighth minute for a last-ditch foul on Alexander Isak.

Pochettino accepted full responsibility for the loss, but claimed the dismissal was wrong and United should have had a penalty moments earlier for a Jérémy Jacquet challenge on Bryan Mbeumo. 'It was a desperate take,"' writes Andy Hunter at Anfield.

#910. Hirst key for Stoke, injuries derail Millwall - Sam Parkin's EFL takeaways

After the last international break of the year, Final Score pundit and former Swindon Town, Luton Town and Northampton Town striker selects his takeaways from the Championship, League One and League Two.

Stoke City are the Championship's form team, having taken 32 points from the last 39, but can they stay the distance in the promotion race?

Parkin: "I think everyone, probably me included, is really optimistic about their chances of this being the season they get it right.

"We're a fair chunk into the season now and I thought today's result was really important because I believe this was their first win over anyone in the top eight. It felt like a bit of a statement win because Birmingham, apart from their defeat at Cardiff, have been really competitive in more or less every game.

"They've been able to just come out the right side of the scoreline and they've had to rely on their goalkeeper [Viktor] Johansson, who I think is one of the top goalkeepers at this level.

"I think there was an early shift in formation, going to a back three in the early part of the campaign, and I think that's proved quite important. They're keeping clean sheets and they've got a goalscorer in George Hirst.

"I read a lot about Stoke City fans saying they're still probably short on forwards who are going to get them the goals. I know that [Jack] McGlynn has chipped in with a really impressive number from midfield, but for Hirst to get that big winning goal, that will have done his confidence the world of good.

"He's been promoted previously with Ipswich and there's no reason why he can't be Stoke's main man up front."

Millwall have slumped to 16th after fighting for promotion in the last few seasons and they have lost five of their last seven league games.

Parkin: "They've had to deal with a horrendous injury crisis. It was at a level that I was struggling to think of a comparable club in the early part of the season. They were just having players go down week after week.

"There was one game in particular I covered against Wrexham and they had the walking wounded (out there), so I think they're still recovering from that.

"They've got some of the main players in [Casper] De Norre back fit now and available, but I think [Josh] Coburn was unavailable again today, and [Mihailo] Ivanovic is just making his way back - I would say they are three of their more important players.

"Take away [Jake] Cooper at the back, who's been a mainstay for a number of years, and I think that trio I've just mentioned are so fundamental to their chances this season.

"They're still playing catch up to a degree, but Alex Neil has not pulled any punches in some of his interviews and he'll be disappointed.

"On the flip side of that, QPR are in a really good place at the moment, and are a much tougher proposition than maybe they would have been over the last couple of seasons.

"I think Millwall will improve over time. I don't see them emulating what they did last season, but I think they can be optimistic they can get some better results once everyone's back available."

Lincoln City management duo Chris Cohen and Tom Shaw

Lincoln City are finding life in the Championship tough after romping to the League One title last season and they have lost seven of their last nine league games.

Parkin: "It's been a downward spiral and the home form's a bit of an issue. They just have the one win over Burnley there - and Burnley were in dire straits when they came.

"They've lost four in a row so that will be a little bit of a concern because they found a formula on the road in the early part of the season. But, yeah, you've got to do better in your home form.

"I still trust they're going to be competitive and the majority of that squad, Jack Moylan apart, is still there from last season. You don't get over 100 points and then lose everything.

"That's always going to count for something when you've got the nucleus of that squad still together, even if it is in a higher division. So I think the spirit will remain amongst that group, despite the recent defeats.

"They've got to start taking points off the better teams in the division as well. All their victories have come against teams who are in the lower part of the table, like Preston and Burnley.

"They won at Bolton and at Bristol City, so they're not really mixing it with the teams in the top half of the table at the moment.

"But I think the bottom line is the management duo would have absolutely taken being five points above 22nd at this stage of the season, so they've given themselves a good opportunity to stay in the division."

Barnsley are four points from safety at the bottom of League One after Friday's defeat by Sheffield Wednesday in the South Yorkshire derby and are on course for a first return to the fourth tier since 1979.

Parkin: "I think on last night's evidence, they're a better team than the league table suggests. That's an absolute certainty in my mind.

"My one concern is where are the goals going to come from? For all their dangerous play, which is incredibly aggressive and energetic, with and without the ball, where are the goals?

"They throw caution to the wind and there's a real energy and youth about the side, which I actually really admired in defeat.

"It's just translating all that into goals and that was obviously one part of it against Wednesday, and giving away bad goals - they've conceded the most set pieces now in the division.

"They conceded in that manner again, and because they play such a high line, they (also) get exposed by teams on the counter. Maybe that's a little bit of naivety. Maybe that's a little bit lack of experience, which they can go some way to mending in January when the transfer window opens.

"But they may be adrift at the bottom if they don't turn things around soon. In short, I think they're a better team than a relegated team. But the most important thing in football, as we know, is putting the ball in the back of the net and that clearly is a problem for them at the moment."

Crawley Town's Dylan Morgan celebrates scoring against Cheltenham Town

Crawley Town boosted their chances of staying in the EFL when they recorded their first home league win of the season over Fleetwood Town and they have generated some momentum in their last few matches.

Parkin: "Former Leeds and Sheffield United manager Kevin Blackwell is in charge now till the end of the season. I was injured for the majority of his spell at Luton Town when he was my manager, but I'm kind of well versed in his methods and he will make them really hard to beat.

"That's always the first thing you want when you take over a struggling side, you need to stop shipping goals. You need to get them organised. You need to work on set-pieces and be a threat on that front. He will do all those things.

"I think the three results in the league, two wins and a draw, have showed you that his methods have already come to fruition. His approach will be very different to probably what the players were being asked to do under Scott Lindsey.

"It'll be a different kind of football. They'll play long at times, they'll want to play in the opposition's half. I think in terms of a plan to get survival, he could very well be the man to supply that.

"They've chosen him after he was initially brought in as interim manager because the performances have improved across the last few weeks, despite the embarrassment of the FA Cup defeat to Wimborne.

"He's made them competitive very quickly and I think a lot of teams are going to be in for a real game when they face them."

Sam Parkin was speaking to BBC Sport England's David Anderson

#909. European football: Doué carried off for PSG while Kane vows to return fresh

Doué injury adds to that of Kvaratskhelia last month

Nice 2-3 PSG; Lazio 3-0 Lecce; Gladbach 0-1 Dortmund

Désiré Doué was carried off in tears after suffering what looked like a nasty knee injury as Paris Saint-Germain beat Nice 3-2 in Ligue 1.

Doué went down after twisting awkwardly late in the first half as he tried to control the ball, shortly after scoring to put PSG 2-1 ahead. The match was stopped for five minutes to allow Doué to receive treatment to his right knee before he was carried off to a backdrop of applause from the crowd at the Allianz Riviera stadium.

PSG will now be dreading discovering the extent of the injury, having lost Khvicha Kvaratskhelia to a ruptured anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee playing against Barcelona last month. The Georgian winger is unlikely to return this season, and Doué looks set for a significant spell on the sidelines too.

“We will need to wait until tomorrow for the test results, but it is obviously a serious injury,” PSG’s coach, Luis Enrique, told the broadcaster Ligue 1+.

Mohamed Amoura had given Nice the lead only for Senny Mayulu to equalise with a penalty awarded after a video assistant referee (VAR) check for a handball.

Doué – who was wearing a mouthguard after one of his teeth became dislodged while playing for France against Italy during the international break – put PSG ahead a minute later, turning in at the back post from an Achraf Hakimi assist for his sixth of the season in all competitions.

His replacement, Ferran Torres, scored PSG’s third in the 85th minute, controlling in the box before finishing on the turn for his eighth goal of the season – but first in two months. Ali Abdi pulled one back for Nice in stoppage time, but their run of three straight wins was ended as PSG made it 12 victories on the bounce.

Lazio will continue their surprise stay at the top of Serie A for at least another week after thumping Lecce 3-0, while a red-hot Donyell Malen scored four at Parma to lift Roma up to second.

Gennaro Gattuso’s Lazio are two points ahead of their local rivals thanks to goals in each half from Tijjani Noslin and a late Davide Frattesi strike. Inter would close to within a point of Lazio with a win at struggling Atalanta on Sunday.

“I am proud of the mentality and the hunger shown today,” said Gattuso to Dazn. “It’s all down to the players, they have the right mentality, hunger and team spirit. What they are doing is incredible.”

Malen took his tally in all competitions for Roma this season to 16 before Wednesday’s daunting Champions League clash at Paris Saint-Germain. The Netherlands forward opened the scoring six minutes before half-time with a brilliant touch and finish, and put Roma, also unbeaten in the league, back in the lead in the 68th minute. Rodrigo Mora added Roma’s third moments later and then Malen capped another superb display with two more expert finishes.

Scott McTominay’s second-half strike gave Napoli a hard-earned 1-0 win over Torino to ease the pressure on manager Massimiliano Allegri, while Como stayed six points behind the leaders in fourth with a 2-0 home win over Cagliari.

In Spain, Kylian Mbappé’s third miss in his last six penalty attempts for club and country did not prove costly as ⁠Carlos Espi’s late winner helped Real Madrid to a 2-1 home victory over Celta Vigo. Real have 33 points from ⁠13 La Liga games, level ⁠with leaders Barcelona, ​but have now played a game more. The Catalans are in action on Sunday at home to Villarreal.

Mbappé’s wastefulness from 12 yards had already ⁠cost Real a point earlier in the season and this time it was almost two as he lifted his effort well over the crossbar. He also ⁠missed a penalty when the Madrid side lost 1-0 at Real Betis in September, and for France ​against Morocco in the World Cup. On both ‌those occasions he shot ‌low and saw his effort saved, which perhaps might explain why he tried to go high ‌this time.

Celta took the lead inside six minutes when Pablo Durán scored from close range as he turned in Williot Swedberg’s low cross. Real had the chance to pull level when Mbappé had his arm pulled by Celta defender Javier Rodriguez and the referee pointed to the spot, but the Frenchman could not convert.

Real were level on 66 minutes when Jude ‌Bellingham drilled the ball low into the net from just inside box. It looked as though they would be frustrated before Espi’s initial header was saved by ​goalkeeper Ionut Radu, but he turned in the rebound.

Kike Salas equalised in added time at the end of the game as Sevilla earned a 1-1 draw with Real Betis in the Seville derby. Antony netted for the visitors early in the second half with his first goal of the season ⁠but Betis were denied a place in the top three by the equaliser.

Deportivo ​Alaves ended an eight-game winless ​streak with a 3-1 home victory ​over Deportivo La Coruna. Angel Perez opened the scoring for the hosts, but ​they were pegged back ‌to 1-1 by ​an own goal from ​Nahuel Tenaglia. Lucas Boye, who earlier missed a penalty, scored Alaves’ second and the points were made safe when Denis Suarez netted in added time. Valencia moved out of the bottom three with a 1-0 away win at Rayo Vallecano thanks to Jose Copete’s first half headed goal.

In Germany, Borussia Dortmund’s Felix Nmecha fired his side to the top of ⁠the Bundesliga table as they won 1-0 at bottom side Borussia Mönchengladbach. After Bayern Munich ⁠were held to ⁠a ​1-1 draw at home by Cologne on Friday, Dortmund capitalised to take a two-point lead at the summit.

The home side played far better ⁠than their position would suggest, ​withstanding waves of pressure ‌from the visitors, ‌but Gladbach finally cracked in the 80th minute when Nmecha picked ‌up the ball on the edge of a packed penalty area and let fly. Unsighted by the thicket of bodies in front of him, the goalkeeper Daniel Batz misjudged the trajectory of the ball, and it flew over his right shoulder ‌and into the net.

Gladbach created a number of chances, but Gregor Kobel came to the rescue ​with several fine saves for Dortmund, and once the goal went in, there was no way back for the hosts. Dortmund have 24 points after 10 games, two ahead of Bayern and third-placed Freiburg, who ⁠beat Elversberg 1-0.

Meanwhile, FifPro said it was “deeply concerned” by public comments from Bayern’s leadership about Jamal Musiala’s contract, accusing the German ⁠champions of putting pressure on the midfielder while he recovers from health problems. The global players’ union was responding to recent remarks by senior Bayern officials, including ⁠honorary president Uli Hoeness, ⁠chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen ​and supervisory board member Karl-Heinz Rummenigge, about Musiala’s future at the club.

Hoeness this month questioned whether the 23-year-old Germany international could return to his ⁠previous level after being diagnosed with a neurological disorder. Dreesen later backed those remarks, saying Bayern would evaluate Musiala’s progress and discuss his future with his representatives. Rummenigge subsequently defended ⁠the comments, saying the club’s consideration of Musiala’s health and contract situation was both responsible and normal.

“Bayern’s honorary ​president, chief executive and former chief executive ‌have all publicly questioned Musiala’s contract ‌in quick succession,” Fifpro said in a statement. “In FifPro’s view, this is a coordinated strategy to put ‌pressure on Musiala and his representatives ahead of any negotiations. A club of Bayern’s standing should know better.”

Musiala signed a contract extension with Bayern until 2030 in February last year. He has endured a difficult run of injuries and health setbacks in recent months. He broke his leg at the Club World Cup in July 2025, missed half of last season and collapsed twice within a ‌few days in August before being diagnosed with a neurological disorder. In September, he suffered a hamstring injury.

After September’s injury, Musiala returned as a substitute in Bayern’s 1-1 home draw with Cologne in the Bundesliga on Friday in which Harry Kane sustained an injury that may mean months of rehabilitation. On Saturday, Kane said he was looking to come back improved for “the business end of the season”. Kane tore a ligament in his left ankle and Bayern said the Ballon d’Or winner had undergone “successful surgery overnight” having earlier said that Kane would be out for “the next few months”.

Kane posted a photo on Instagram of himself smiling broadly, while sitting on a hospital bed after the surgery, with his leg encased in a medical boot. “The highs and lows of life!” the 33-year-old wrote. “Obviously very disappointed to get this injury but as always it’s an opportunity to show resilience and improvement going into 2027. I’ll be back fresh and ready to go for the business end of the season.”

#908. Nine wins in a row - Bournemouth & Evanilson continue to make history

Evanilson strikes again as Bournemouth see off Forest

"We have to stick together and face reality."

That is how Bournemouth manager Marco Rose responded after his side had dropped into the Premier League relegation zone with a 5-1 defeat by Chelsea.

Six weeks on, it is an entirely different story.

The Cherries are up to fourth in the top flight, having clinched a club record ninth successive win in all competitions - with five in the league.

It is a far cry from that thumping defeat at Stamford Bridge, which left Rose without a victory in his first six Premier League matches in charge.

Bournemouth earned just three points from those six games (draws against Everton, Newcastle and Brentford - when the Cherries squandered winning positions) and fans may have been fearing the worst.

From the outside looking in, it seemed as though the appointment of Rose might not deliver the fortunes that had been expected.

The 50-year-old, who accepted the unenviable task of succeeding Andoni Iraola, called for his side to take "responsibility" after the defeat by Chelsea.

"Three points after six games, we need a reaction. Everyone has to take responsibility to do better," said Rose at the time.

"We knew it was going to be a demanding season. We have to stick together and face reality. The reality is we have three points after six games."

The Cherries have not only responded to Rose's rallying cry, they have exceeded all expectations.

Those nine straight wins include five in the league - and his side are now only four points behind second-placed Brighton.

After easing to a 2-0 victory against Nottingham Forest on Saturday, Rose said: "We don't think about records, we just think about the next game.

"We took the right approach. We knew it would be tough and we would have to stay patient, and that's what we did. It was a top performance and a deserved win."

Bournemouth's nine-game winning streak is a club record - beating two separate runs of eight in 1998-99 and 2012-13

Since arriving in England in July, Rose has come across as a composed presence, regardless of Bournemouth's results.

However, the former Borussia Dortmund and RB Leipzig manager was unable to hide his delight at his side's record-breaking victory against Forest.

Shortly after the full-time whistle sounded at the Vitality Stadium, Rose unleashed a series of celebratory fist pumps in front of the delighted home fans.

It was arguably the first time Rose had let down his guard since arriving on the South Coast four months ago - and who could blame him, given the significance of the result?

It is the first time in the club's history they have won five consecutive Premier League matches.

The prospect of securing European football for a second consecutive season is growing by the week.

In addition to wins over Sunderland, Manchester United, Leeds, Ipswich and Nottingham Forest in the Premier League, Bournemouth have beaten AC Milan in the Europa League and Aston Villa in the League Cup.

Their remarkable run of nine wins across all competitions surpasses their previous record of eight, achieved in both the 1998-99 and 2012-13 seasons.

Bournemouth are currently also second in the Europa League league phase and are one of only three teams to have won all four of their matches so far.

"Tonight I will smile, but not just because of the table - because we win," Rose told Match of the Day.

Meanwhile, Justin Kluivert - who scored Bournemouth's second goal against Forest - urged his team-mates to remain "humble" and "not settle for less" before upcoming matches against Celta Vigo and Fulham.

'I'll call him' - Justin Kluivert happy he's scored same week as dad Patrick

One of the main reasons behind Bournemouth's upturn in form has been the hot streak forward Evanilson is currently enjoying.

After failing to find the back of the net in his first five appearances of the season, the Brazilian became the first player in club history to score in six consecutive Premier League matches when he broke the deadlock against Forest.

Since joining the Cherries in a club record deal from Porto in August 2024, the 27-year-old has struggled for consistency.

In his first season in England, Evanilson managed 10 goals and five assists in 31 league appearances.

Last season, though, was less productive for the forward, who managed only six goals and three assists in 36 top-flight appearances.

By scoring against Forest, Evanilson has already matched his return from the previous campaign.

"He is lovely, he works hard and his quality does the rest," said Kluivert. "I am happy he has been scoring, and working hard for the team."

It is not only goals that Evanilson is providing for his side this season. He has also proven that he is able to drop between the lines - and out wide - to allow Bournemouth to be a fluid side in transition.

That was evident for the Cherries' second goal against Forest, when Evanilson pulled out to the left touchline and threaded the ball down the line for Marcus Tavernier to cross for the unmarked Kluivert in the centre.

"The way he works for us out of possession, works as a link player and goes deep," added Rose. "The way he scores is quite impressive."

The season has not even reached the halfway point, so no-one at Bournemouth will be getting carried away just yet.

What is possible for the Cherries this term will largely depend on what happens - or, perhaps more importantly, what does not happen - in January.

Bournemouth's impressive recent form - and that of certain individuals - is likely to attract attention from some of the biggest clubs in the Premier League when the transfer window opens in January.

Players such as Evanilson, Rayan, Alex Scott and Junior Kroupi, in particular, are likely to be the subject of interest from elsewhere.

So what should Bournemouth do if some of the Premier League's 'bigger' clubs come knocking for their crown jewels?

Should they resist the premium prices the mid-season market is likely to bring and keep hold of their star quality to preserve their own aspirations this season?

Former Manchester City and England goalkeeper Joe Hart believes the Cherries should try to keep hold of their stars to bolster their own hopes this term - insisting the "sky is the limit" for Rose's side.

"Rather than setting a specific target, like Champions League qualification, they should just enjoy what they are doing," Hart told BBC Sport.

"It is crucial they keep everyone fit and firing, given they have the extra demands of playing in Europe plus the busy Christmas period to come.

"Junior Kroupi and Alex Scott came off the bench today, and that kind of squad depth could be massive for them.

"It is all about keeping themselves in the running because a lot of teams are stumbling right now, whereas Bournemouth are really in a rich vein of form."

#907. Aston Villa held at home as dogged Sunderland battle for Régis Le Bris

For Aston Villa, a painful stalemate at home to Sunderland, but for Régis Le Bris and his players, this was another triumph of sorts. The raw numbers spoke volumes of Villa’s struggles against a defence that backed themselves to keep Unai Emery’s side at bay. All but one of Villa’s seven shots on target came from outside the visitors’ box and the one inside it, courtesy of Ian Maatsen, was forgettable. Owing to a summer of change, injuries and Emery resting John McGinn with Tuesday’s game at Galatasaray in mind, Maatsen, incredibly, was the sole survivor in the Villa starting XI from when these sides played out a 4-3 classic seven months ago.

Villa were too predictable, short of a spark, someone to unpick an organised back line. Johan Manzambi, Emi Buendía and Alysson all flattered to deceive on an afternoon when Ibrahim Mbaye and McGinn arrived from the bench. Alejandro Garnacho, however, was not involved in Villa’s matchday squad for the second successive match and the Chelsea loanee has played just 38 minutes in the Premier League this campaign. Tammy Abraham, the match-winner in April, was also left out and a January move looks likely.

“I am trying to select the players I think that are ready to play and the selection is thinking for the best of the team,” said Emery, who was again reluctant to blame the empty North Stand as a factor behind their disappointing home form, a sharp contrast to their 11-game winning run here last season. “In my experiences here and in Spain, when they [stadiums] are in works like we are in now, it’s a small sacrifice, but it’s not an excuse,” Villa’s manager added. “We have to play with this situation and next year it will be better.”

Villa’s frustration was underlined by a moment on the verge of half-time, when Emery gave Sunderland’s kit man, Luke Purcell, a gentle shove on the sidelines in an attempt to speed up a Villa restart. “We have increased our demands a lot, our level, but still there are favourites in front of us, to reach the top six, top four,” Emery said. “We are now again in a new construction with some new players who are sharing their qualities and we are trying to mix different players, young players to build our structure as fast as possible.”

With 90 minutes and 25 seconds showing on the big screens, Chemsdine Talbi almost snatched victory for Sunderland, the Moroccan winger shaving the upright of Zion Suzuki’s goal with a spell-bending strike. Talbi did almost everything right, bursting past Aaron Wan-Bissaka, comfortably eliminating the defender, before using Boubacar Kamara as a mannequin to get his bearings, but his curling right-foot shot was ultimately a few inches too close to the post. For Villa, a first clean sheet in the league here since March, but this draw extended their winless run to five matches in all competitions.

For Sunderland, this may not have been the dopamine hit of beating Chelsea, but it was was another gutsy showing, and without two key players in Granit Xhaka and Brian Brobbey, both of whom were absent through injury. It was a big team performance, another feather in the cap of Jules Ahoka, the 20-year-old midfielder who shone on his first Premier League start. Ahoka started last season playing on sandy pitches in the Democratic Republic of Congo’s second division. “He is getting better game after game,” Le Bris said.

Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football

Sunderland were happy to soak up the Villa pressure. Emery introduced the 17-year-old Brian Madjo, who trained with England under-21s during the international break, but in place of Nicolas Jackson rather than to join him in attack. By which point Mbaye had entered and combined with McGinn to fashion another nearly moment. Disbelief reigned in the stands, but had Talbi located the top corner, things could have felt a lot worse at the final whistle.

#906. 'Fragile' and 'miles off it' - Alonso's Chelsea honeymoon is over

Leeds dominate Chelsea for first Stamford Bridge win since 1999

Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso is already in firefighting mode.

His team were booed by their own supporters at several points during a dominant 4-1 Leeds victory at Stamford Bridge, their first win there since 1999.

The first negative reaction came at half-time while the score was still 1-1. The ground then began to empty after the third and fourth Leeds goals, and the fans remaining voiced their dissent once more at the final whistle.

Although there were mitigating circumstances, including a potentially harsh penalty decision against them and the loss of midfielder Moises Caicedo to injury, joining a five-strong list of players on the treatment table, the defeat was thoroughly deserved.

It leaves Chelsea with three losses in their past four Premier League matches and they have slipped from fifth place to eighth, already 14 points behind league leaders Arsenal.

In October, Tottenham won at Stamford Bridge for only the second time in the Premier League era, while the 1-0 defeat at bottom club Sunderland before the international break was another alarm bell.

It is the first time in 67 years that Chelsea have lost at home to both Leeds and Spurs in the same season.

"We need to find solutions, for sure, because there will be setbacks during any game," Alonso said after the match.

"To be able to go through that and to know that it's still so long to play, it's something mandatory in this competition and today I felt that probably we are in a fragile moment mentally.

"When we received a punch we didn't recover that strongly."

Okafor double delivers rare win for Leeds at Chelsea

'Officials can't use common sense' - was Rogers handball correct?

Indeed, even when Chelsea have been winning matches, they have often looked unconvincing.

Yet Blues supporters chanted their new manager's name and seemed optimistic after the summer transfer business - despite a disappointing 10th-place finish last season.

Club record Â£117m signing Morgan Rogers was joined by the experienced trio of Emiliano Martinez, Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson.

It was the clinical finishing of Rogers, along with Cole Palmer and Joao Pedro earlier in the season, that masked the underlying fragility of Alonso's team.

Before this weekend, the Blues ranked 14th for expected goal difference and were joint 12th in Opta's expected points table.

After their latest setback, ex-England forward and BBC Match of the Day pundit Alan Shearer said: "Chelsea were all over the place. Once Moises Caicedo went off injured early on, there was no physicality and they looked weak.

"They hardly created anything going forward and the back four didn't look comfortable. There was no desire, cohesion or fight from the home side, but we shouldn't take anything away from Leeds.

"Two weeks ago Chelsea were bullied by Sunderland centre-forward Brian Brobbey and they let Dominic Calvert-Lewin do the same today, which is alarming.

"It's fair to say Xabi Alonso's honeymoon period is over. He needs to tell his players this simply isn't good enough. They are miles off it and have to do better in every department."

Xabi Alonso post-match interview - Chelsea v Leeds United

Xabi Alonso was appointed Chelsea manager on a four-year deal in May

In Alonso's defence, Chelsea had problems before his arrival.

They finished 10th last season, having been outrun in 37 of their 38 matches, and had three managers during a chaotic campaign.

Remarkably, Chelsea have seven more points from corresponding fixtures this season and last, but it mostly serves to show how low the bar was set.

Champions League qualification was again the club's pre-season target and Alonso's appointment was designed to bring stability and authority.

The former Real Madrid and Liverpool midfielder had an impressive playing career and earned much early admiration as a manager, guiding Bayer Leverkusen to a league and cup double in 2024.

However, the Spaniard, who was sacked by Real Madrid last season, has yet to establish any real consistency - beyond his defence leaking goals regularly.

Only Crystal Palace, Coventry City and Ipswich Town have conceded more goals than Chelsea this season.

Chelsea are also now averaging fewer than a goal per game since Joao Pedro suffered a thigh injury in training. Alongside Pedro and now Caicedo, Jorrel Hato, Maxence Lacroix, Reece James and Jamie Gittens are also injured.

It highlights how they have gained little benefit of having a season without European football.

Alonso is also beginning to face criticism from sections of the fanbase for both his team selections and substitutions.

Chief among the reasons is the constant chopping and changing of the starting XI, having now made 28 line-up changes (behind only Tottenham) while also switching between back-four and back-three systems.

In addition, Alonso is being criticised for his use of personnel, having deployed Pedro Neto as a striker on two occasions and, some would argue, not made enough use of exciting young winger Estevao.

Chelsea have shown 'no progression' under Alonso - Shearer

Against Leeds he gave striker Emmanuel Emegha his first start alongside Estevao and, although the Dutch striker scored, the pair were the first players he substituted while Chelsea were chasing the game at 3-1 down.

Similarly, his late in-game interventions are under scrutiny, including the decision to bring on striker Welbeck only in the 90th minute of the defeat by Spurs.

He took until the 64th minute to make changes against Leeds when Chelsea were already 3-1 down. Only three clubs had made more substitutions in the last 15 minutes than Chelsea in the league this season.

Given Leeds' strengths, Chelsea should have been better prepared for what was coming. Before kick-off, Leeds had applied more high-intensity pressures in the opposition half than any other team in the Premier League.

They had also generated the most expected goals from set-pieces and won the most duels. Leeds maintained those trends at Stamford Bridge against a Chelsea side often accused of being soft.

Chelsea have had problems in recent seasons, but this was still their worst home defeat since a 4-1 loss to Brentford in 2022.

Likewise, it is almost uncharted territory in Alonso's managerial career, having only previously lost at home by a three-goal margin once.

The stadium emptied and supporters again left early.

Players displayed negative body language and argued with one another both during the match and after the final whistle.

As a result, Alonso has gone from needing to fix defensive issues to dealing with problems that appear to be spreading throughout the squad.

#905. 37 years after fall of Berlin Wall: How divided are Germans?

Three artists share their thoughts on the reunification of East and West Germany. How do they perceive a shared "we" and what gives them cause for optimism?

When the Berlin Wall fell on November 9, 1989, ending East Germany's isolation from the West, the event was celebrated on both sides of the border. Yet, 37 years later, many people on both sides remain deeply skeptical of each other.

Surveys show that only a minority of respondents report feeling a strong sense of community between those from former East and West Germany, and many continue to perceive significant differences.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

We asked three artists from Germany with different perspectives on the history of the country's division to share their views.

Author Lea Streisand was born in 1979 and experienced the fall of the Berlin Wall firsthand while growing up in East Berlin.

In her books and essays, she has returned to her East German upbringing many times, using literature to process it.

The novel "Hufeland, at the corner of Bötzow" (2019, Ullstein), for example, recounts the period of reunification from a child's perspective.

"November 9, 1989, was simply incredible," she told DW. She was 10 years old at the time. When her mother bought her winter boots with the 100 Deutsche Marks she received from the West German state — a welcome gift given to all East German citizens — she was so disappointed that she felt like crying. But later, a friend of her parents' let her buy so many sweets at the supermarket that they lasted until Christmas.

"The disappointment really set in afterwards, with what happened over the course of the following year. It was unbelievable how quickly an entire system was suddenly swept away and a new one built up, as if to say, 'There you go. You're welcome'," Streisand recalled. "I think it was just too fast for people."

The people of East Germany, or the GDR, had brought about the fall of the Berlin Wall themselves through a civil rights movement and numerous demonstrations. For many, however, the goal was not to dissolve the state immediately but to reform it.

Among them was Anke Feuchtenberger, born in 1963 in East Berlin. Her childhood was spent in East Berlin and in the East German region of Western Pomerania, where she now lives again and feels "very much at home."

Today, she teaches at the University of Applied Sciences in Hamburg, meaning she spends time on both sides of the former divide. Feuchtenberger is often described as Germany's most influential comic artist. Her work has also garnered international acclaim.

"Back then, as artists, we tried to bring about a change through posters and flyers — to gain more freedom without immediately abolishing socialism," she explained.

At the time, the fall of the Berlin Wall stirred up mixed feelings in Feuchtenberger: "I soon realized that the creative and revolutionary aspects of our movement were very quickly being smothered by consumerism, and that nationalist tendencies — which had already been noticeable before — were coming to the fore," Feuchtenberger recalled. "That made me afraid."

Meanwhile, for photographic artist Simon Menner, born in 1978 in Emmendingen, in the West German state of Baden-Württemberg, Berlin was very far away. As Menner put it, he experienced the fall of the Berlin Wall as a child in a "rather abstract" way. Today, Berlin is his home.

In his experience, the way films and documentaries portrayed East Germany around the time of reunification was very bleak. "But West Germany in the '80s," he said, "was also bleak and very staid."

This uneven portrayal of the two parts of Germany is an issue that deeply concerns Menner — partly because he unwittingly contributed to it in a small way. Among other things, Menner's work explores the topic of surveillance and how it works.

In the archives of East Germany's Ministry for State Security, or Stasi — which are freely accessible today as part of the National Archives — he discovered a massive collection of photographs that both fascinated and horrified him and which he wanted to bring to the attention of a wider public.

His photo book "Top Secret" (2012, from publisher Hatje Cantz) features a selection of photos that offer a unique insight into the work of the Stasi. Some are eerie, while others are curious or even absurd.

Menner also tried to look into the photo archive of West Germany's Federal Intelligence Service. "I spent a year trying to gain access — without success," he said.

In hindsight, he now finds his artistic project problematic because he believes it is too one-sided, focusing exclusively on East Germany's past.

According to Menner, West Germany's intelligence services in the 1960s were not exactly models of virtue either, and he believes it is "actually high time" to critically examine this part of history as well. In his view, an honest examination of Germany's past as a whole is a prerequisite for genuine reconciliation.

Streisand believes literature can help foster mutual understanding. "Literature opens a window into experiences we haven't had ourselves," she said. "You can immerse yourself in the mind of someone who has had a different life than you have and understand what happened."

Interest in these stories remains strong. In 2023, Feuchtenberger published the nearly 500-page graphic novel "Comrade Cuckoo" (published by Reprodukt), which was the first graphic novel to be nominated for the Leipzig Book Fair Prize in the fiction category.

The story spans a childhood in the fictional East German village of Pritschitanow in the 1960s in the GDR to the post-Reunification era. In it, Feuchtenberger weaves autobiographical memories of her upbringing with fantastical and fictional elements.

The artist said she was surprised "that, so long after the fall of the wall, my stories have sparked such great interest in the West."

In particular, the fact that the main character, Kerstin, rarely sees her parents because they both work full-time is a topic that often comes up at readings. In the GDR, everyone had the right to work, she said. At the same time, it was a civic duty.

Could the West German interest in this stem from the fact that full-time employment for both parents has long been less common in the West? It's possible, said Feuchtenberger.

When looking toward their shared future, the two East German women are more optimistic than Menner, from West Germany.

"In Berlin, I often don't even notice anymore whether I'm in the West or the East," said Menner. "But when it comes to sociopolitical issues, politicians should listen to older and younger people more closely," he added, referring to the recent election successes of far-right Alternative for Germany, or AfD . "Otherwise, things are going to get difficult in the near future."

"It's very important to step outside our own bubble because people all over the world are facing problems. Constantly focusing on this German-German divide that has emerged between the groups doesn't help," said Feuchtenberger.

"For me personally, the whole issue of borders has somehow dissolved," she explained. This is due in no small part to the many trips abroad that have taken her to various places around the world.

Moreover, in her hometown near the Polish border, she observes how animals couldn't care less about the border. "They come from the east and the west and do whatever they want," she said. That's why she also gave "Comrade Cuckoo" the working title "A German Animal in a German Forest," "because I found the absurdity of an animal having a nationality so funny."

"This East-West thing — our children won't have any interest in it at all," said Streisand. "Young people don't care where their parents come from. Can I get a job that will support a family? Do I have to go to war? Right now, completely different things are relevant."

This article was originally written in German.

#904. Nicole Richie Reveals Daughter Kate Has “Surpassed” Her in This Way

Nicole Richie shared that when it comes to the world of beauty, her and husband Joel Madden's 18-year-old daughter Harlow Kate Madden has completely eclipsed her mom.

Nicole Richie has a simple solution for her beauty needs.

The Simple Life alum revealed that her and husband Joel Madden’s 18-year-old daughter Harlow Kate Madden has become her go-to makeup artist, as the teen is even more skilled than she is in that particular area.

“I would say that she has surpassed me,” Richie told People in an interview published Nov. 19. “She’s so good. I actually am not very good at doing my own makeup. She is a whole different animal.”

And the 45-year-old knows exactly how her daughter—who chooses to go by her middle name Kate—got so good at glowing up her family.

“She grew up watching YouTube tutorials,” Richie explained, “and she’s so well-versed in makeup and contour and highlighting and just all the things.”

“If I ever need my makeup done at home, I’m going to her,” the House of Harlow founder added. “It’s not me doing it ... She kills a cat-eye.”

Of course, Kate will soon be showing off more of her talents as she officially builds the foundation for a modeling career after signing with The Lions Management.

“I’ve always dreamed of modeling, so getting to start this next chapter with The Lions is incredibly exciting,” Kate shared in a Nov. 20 statement to Women’s Wear Daily. “Fashion has always been a way for me to express myself, and I can’t wait to explore that in a whole new way.”

She added, “I’m looking forward to learning, growing, meeting new people, and seeing where this journey takes me.”

Kate made her modeling debut alongside her mom for Balenciaga’s recent campaign celebrating the 25th anniversary of their Le City handbag, a style Richie was particularly fond of in the early 2000s.

And Madden—who also shares son Sparrow James Midnight, 17, with Richie—was particularly thrilled to see his daughter achieving her dream.

The Good Charlotte frontman reposted Kate’s modeling announcement to his Instagram Stories Nov. 20, captioning it with three red heart emojis and writing in all caps, “KATE!”

#903. Evanilson and Kluivert sink Forest to earn Bournemouth ninth win in a row

Marco Rose saluted the in-form Evanilson after the Brazilian scored for a sixth Premier League game in a row to lift Bournemouth up to fourth place with a 2-0 win over Nottingham Forest.

Evanilson’s brilliantly taken 19th-minute opener set his side on course for a club record ninth straight win in all competitions, while the defeat means Forest are only above the relegation places on goal difference having failed to build on the momentum of their 3-1 win against Manchester City before the international break.

Rose said: “We defend together as a team, and we attack together as a team, but the forward guys were excellent today. They did a great job scoring the goals and the other guys support them. Evanilson creates space, carries the ball, provides assists and now he scores goals as a No 9, really beautiful goals so I am happy.”

Both teams started the game on the front foot and Forest had the first sight of goal. Neco Williams nodded dangerously across the face of goal at the far post, but Liam Delap was beaten to the ball by home defender Antonio Silva.

Evanilson was denied by a brilliant last-ditch tackle from Forest centre-back Jair Cunha before Marcus Tavernier’s 20-yard curler was well saved by Matz Sels.

Bournemouth took the lead in the 19th minute. James Hill cushioned a header into the path of Evanilson, and the Brazilian took one touch before blasting a left-foot shot into the roof of the net.

Justin Kluivert almost doubled the home side’s lead with an effort from 20 yards which sailed narrowly over the crossbar. Evanilson then failed to keep his shot down after a long throw from Hill caused chaos in the Forest penalty area.

Oliver Glasner’s side had a penalty appeal waved away when Adam Smith blocked Williams’s effort into the arm of teammate Tyler Adams. But Kluivert did make it 2-0 on the stroke of half-time with a simple far-post finish after a superb run and cross from Tavernier.

Forest were much improved in the second half, adopting a more direct approach in a bid to find a way back into the game. Delap turned provider by whipping in a cross for Morgan Gibbs-White but the captain could not properly connect with his header.

Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football

• Bournemouth have won five successive games in the top-flight of English football for the first time. Only Arsenal (67, before Newcastle game) and Manchester City (60) have collected more Premier League points in 2026 than the Cherries (52 – W13 D13 L4).

• Bournemouth have won each of their last nine games in all competitions, their longest ever such run, overtaking two separate runs of eight in 1998-99 and 2012-13.

• Nottingham Forest failed to score in this game despite registering 2.14 expected goals, the highest xG tally by any team not to score in a Premier League match this season. Opta

James McAtee ballooned an effort over the bar as the visitors continued to misfire in front of goal. The substitute Chris Wood also miscued a header from a corner when he should have at least tested the underworked Bournemouth goalkeeper, Djordje Petrovic.

Bournemouth always looked a threat on the counter and Kluivert came close to his second and Bournemouth’s third when he stung the gloves of Sels from 18 yards out. Kluivert should also have been more clinical when he found himself within finishing range but unselfishly laid the ball off to Rayan and the chance went begging.

Glasner, whose side had 19 shots but only one on target, said: “Of course when you lose it’s always a tough 90 minutes, especially when you make too many mistakes like we did in the first half.

“The second goal straight before half-time was a little bit of a killer but credit to the lads in the second half for finding a filter back into the game. We had some good situations, but we couldn’t convert them.

“We are not able to score in this game, and this is what we have to look at and where we have to improve. We took too many touches, and were not so aggressive.”

#902. Fernandez dropped, Anderson scores - Man City's £327m midfield dilemma

Man City drop points to Fulham despite superb Anderson volley

There may have been some eyebrows raised before kick-off when Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca decided to drop club record signing Enzo Fernandez to the bench against Fulham.

Fernandez's lengthy excursions back home to Argentina for their two fixtures during the international break may have been a factor in Maresca's thinking when selecting his starting XI for this game.

If it was, the Italian refrained from giving that as a reason. "I just think for this game it's better having Ayyoub Bouaddi in there," he told TNT Sports shortly before kick-off.

Even so, the move was a significant one as his side were in desperate need of victory after suffering three straight Premier League defeats. That winless streak extended to four after being held to a 1-1 draw.

Maresca had an opportunity to fix the issues in his set-up during the two-week break and admitted on Friday he was searching for "more balance" in the "defensive line, midfield and up front".

The pairing of the steady Bouaddi and all-action Elliot Anderson in the centre of the park was the crucial call, and it may have given Maresca some idea as to how to approach the forthcoming run of games.

"Ayyoub with Elliot were both really good," said Maresca. "Today we used Elliot a bit more attacking midfielder, he arrived inside the box and scored a fantastic goal, he had three or four moments around the box where he was really dangerous.

"It is another solution for us. In this moment, we are trying to know each other more as players and also to find the right solution."

Anderson rescues Man City point against Fulham

Anderson steps up, Berge impresses - player ratings for Man City v Fulham

Elliot Anderson and Ayyoub Bouaddi both joined Manchester City in the summer

Loud jeers greeted the full-time whistle at Etihad Stadium, a culmination of the feeling that was brewing from the home supporters throughout the game.

There was a nervous tension from the beginning, which seemed to seep on to the players on the pitch.

City displayed a flat first-half performance in which they fell behind courtesy of Rodrigo Muniz's superb curling effort, and they needed a stunning second-half volley from Anderson to rescue a point.

The England international is restricted to sitting in front of the back four when Fernandez is in the side, but has the licence to roam when Bouaddi is deployed beside him.

Aside from scoring a spectacular first Premier League goal for City, Anderson created a match-high three chances and had a 100% success rate from 16 passes in the final third of the pitch.

He also had more touches in the opposition box (7), contested more duels than any other player (17) and no-one else managed to win possession back more times than him.

After dragging his side level, another marauding run into the box was snuffed out by the visiting defenders before Rayan Cherki was brought on, which meant Anderson had to retreat back down the pitch.

Maresca needed to change things in order to apply some fresh impetus in the attacking third, but the substitution of Cherki for Phil Foden seemed to limit Anderson's capabilities.

"It's not a good result, especially off the back of three losses," former City goalkeeper Joe Hart told BBC Sport. "There was some good stuff in there.

"It felt like Elliot Anderson was going to take the game by the scruff of the neck but then Cherki came on and took his position. So he [Anderson] didn't have as much of an impact on the game.

"I understood the change - when the lines are deep, there were chances of Cherki unlocking Fulham, but they just defended so well and they also offered a threat on the break."

Leno hopes Hart has his back on MOTD tonight...

City overhauled their midfield to the tune of Â£327m with the signings of trio Fernandez, Anderson and Bouaddi.

The Â£125m club record acquisition Fernandez had made the 14,000-mile round-trip from Manchester to Buenos Aires for Argentina's friendlies against Uruguay and Costa Rica.

The trip allowed him to take the opportunity to pay a visit to boyhood club River Plate, but it is at his current club where there are question marks as to how he fits into the side.

Bouaddi's presence provides more insurance in front of the defence and the 19-year-old Moroccan has the ability to keep the ball ticking.

It means Anderson can play his natural game - but where, then, does Fernandez fit in?

The number 10 position tends to be occupied by either Cherki or Foden, while Maresca pointed out in his pre-match news conference that City "won games with Enzo and lost games with Enzo".

But the manager clearly has to work out how to get the best out of Fernandez, who was given the final five minutes against Fulham in place of Bouaddi.

"There is no point in having a brilliant squad like Manchester City if you are not going to take that into account," said Hart.

"It's very much understandable, if you're going to have a squad and you trust everyone - if someone's done the travelling, he has done the game time, you have got to expect to not use him as much."

City host Napoli in the Champions League on Tuesday followed by a huge trip to Arsenal next Sunday, knowing they could head to the Emirates eight points behind the champions.

Maresca added: "For sure we don't like these kind of moments in terms of four games in a row without a win

"We also know that, unfortunately, it is normal or part of the path, you go through these kind of moments. It is important that we find a way to keep clean sheets that sometimes you need to win games 1-0 for a small difference."

Mikel Arteta's men know all about that and City now need to take a leaf out of their book.

#901. ‘Fragile’ Chelsea must toughen up after Leeds humiliation, admits Xabi Alonso

Xabi Alonso is straying towards crisis territory. Here’s a mind-bending statistic: Chelsea are eighth but have now lost more league games than Manchester United. They were bullied by a rampant Leeds United, who fully merited their first win at Stamford Bridge since going top with a 2-0 victory in December 1999, and can look forward to another season with no European football if they do not sharpen up soon.

It is not really worth dwelling on the fact that the second Leeds goal, a Dominic Calvert-Lewin penalty converted early in an astonishingly one-sided second half, came after Morgan Rogers was harshly penalised for handball. That was a minor detail given the wider picture. Leeds, superbly coached by Daniel Farke and up to sixth after two clinical strikes from Noah Okafor, Calvert-Lewin’s sixth goal of the season and a late effort from Brenden Aaronson, were so dominant that they had no real need for a helping hand from the officials.

Farke’s side were tactically superior against flimsy opposition. For Chelsea, who were jeered off after their fifth defeat in 11 games, the indignities piled high. Records are falling, but not in a good way. This is the first time in 67 years they have lost grudge matches at home to Leeds and Tottenham in the same season, leaving Alonso on shaky ground with supporters, and there was further alarm when Cole Palmer appeared to clash with Willie Isa after the side’s “cultural architect” urged Chelsea’s No 10 to acknowledge the crowd at full-time.

Palmer cut a disgruntled figure throughout and did nothing to make Thomas Tuchel rethink his decision to leave him out of the England squad. The one mitigating factor is that few players will thrive in a directionless team. What does Alonso want Chelsea to be? No one knows. There are no patterns of play and the main takeaway from this surrender is that the only sign of an identity was an addiction to calamitous defending.

Calvert-Lewin followed the lead of Sunderland’s Brian Brobbey by tormenting Levi Colwill and Wesley Fofana. Alonso was appointed in the summer but the pressure is mounting already. The Spaniard’s control even let him down when a ball dropped towards the technical area in the second half.

It was some turnaround from the visitors, who trailed when Emmanuel Emegha marked his full debut by scoring his first goal since joining Chelsea from Strasbourg last summer. Farke continues to excel. The best that can be said of Alonso is that he needs time. Losing Moisés Caicedo early on was a blow. Even then it is impossible to understand Alonso’s intended style of play. There is an emptiness to Chelsea. They faced 21 shots and failed to up the physicality after crumbling against Sunderland.

Admittedly Alonso is dealing with João Pedro’s absence in attack. He has toyed with a false nine in recent weeks, but used a target man this time and the early signs were promising. Emegha gave Chelsea a focal point and finished well when an error from James Justin allowed Rogers to send the striker through on goal.

Leeds were on top when they conceded. Chelsea had lost Caicedo, who made way for Jordan Henderson after injuring his back in a collision with Justin, and were already wobbling. Calvert-Lewin spurned three excellent headed chances and Leeds levelled after 28 minutes.

Chelsea had no defensive leaders. Fofana is too easily ruffled in the air and was involved in the equaliser. He sent a routine header back into dangerous territory and Chelsea panicked. Josh Acheampong mistimed his jump as the ball bounced around and Calvert-Lewin was able to find Okafor, who cut inside and slipped a low shot past Emiliano Martínez.

Farke was rightly disappointed that Leeds were not ahead at half-time. Tarik Muharemovic charged forward from defence, away from Palmer’s feeble challenge, and crossed for Calvert-Lewin to flick wide. Ethan Ampadu ran midfield, outshining Henderson and Romeo Lavia, and the Leeds wing-backs were wonderful. Ao Tanaka went close and Muharemovic grimaced after having a goal disallowed for offside.

Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football

Alonso looked bewildered. Colwill, low on confidence since returning from a knee injury, kept misplacing simple passes and Estêvão Willian was ineffective on the right. Chelsea were jeered off and made a dreadful start to the second half. Martínez should have conceded a penalty for a challenge on Calvert-Lewin. Michael Oliver then pointed to the spot when Rogers was adjudged to have handled Jayden Bogle’s shot.

• Leeds have won their first game against Chelsea at Stamford Bridge in all competitions since December 1999, ending a run of 10 away games against the Blues without victory (D2 L8), while they’ve scored 4+ goals away at Chelsea for the first time since January 1970 (5-2).

• Leeds have won their first Premier League game in London since May 2022 (2-1 against Brentford), ending a run of 15 matches in the Capital without victory (D4 L11), while it’s their biggest winning margin in London since April 2003 (6-1 against Charlton).

• Leeds’ Ao Tanaka (pictured with Cole Palmer) committed three fouls inside the first six minutes against Chelsea; no player has ever fouled more often inside six minutes in a Premier League game on record (since 2003-04). Opta

It looked harsh given Rogers’ arm was close to his body and the ball hit him close to the shoulder but the decision was upheld after a VAR check. Calvert-Lewin stepped up to score and the result was never in doubt once Leeds led. Chelsea, who were mentally fragile, crumbled. Leeds were rampant. Chelsea could not cope with Ampadu’s long throws. One was half cleared but Sean Longstaff worked the ball back to Ampadu, who crossed for Okafor to make it 3-1.

“We are in a fragile moment mentally,” Alonso said. “When we receive a punch we didn’t recover. The fans were disappointed because the expectations are high. I understand their disappointment. There were moments that we were not competing at the level required.”

The closing stages were miserable for Chelsea, who have already conceded 20 goals. Leeds cruised and completed the humiliation when Aaronson, a late substitute, turned past Malo Gusto before sliding a shot through Martínez’s grasp.

The home sections had already emptied out. Those who stayed soon made their displeasure clear.

#900. Raya set to have scan on injury - how much would Arsenal miss him?

David Raya has made 163 appearances since joining Arsenal in 2023

Injuries are never good news, but Arsenal's latest one to first-choice goalkeeper David Raya has come in the worst possible position.

The 31-year-old was forced to leave the pitch 70 minutes into Saturday's 2-2 draw with Newcastle, appearing to hurt his shoulder in an innocuous challenge with Magpies forward William Osula.

The Gunners arguably have the best depth in the league with at least two quality options in all outfield positions after a period of squad strengthening.

In goal, however, cover appears much thinner.

Raya was a key component in Arsenal's Premier League title-winning campaign last season, was named in the Fifpro Men's World 11 and was unlucky to not win the Yashin Trophy, awarded to the world's best goalkeeper, which went to Spain team-mate Unai Simon.

Behind him, Kepa Arrizabalaga still holds the record as the most expensive goalkeeper in football history following his Â£72m move from Athletic Bilbao to Chelsea in August 2018, but is far behind Raya in terms of quality.

Raya's passing range and ability on the ball are key to how Arsenal build their attacks, and his presence is a big reason why they have the best defence in the league.

They have conceded just seven Premier League goals this season, with only Brighton able to match that tally - having played a game fewer.

Arsenal also brought in former Leeds goalkeeper Illan Meslier on a free transfer in the summer but his only appearance this season came in the embarrassing Carabao Cup defeat by League Two Fleetwood.

When asked about Raya's injury, Arteta said he did not know how severe the issue is.

"Well, unfortunately, he had to come off, which is never good news," said Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta.

"He will get assessed now, and probably he will have an MRI [scan] tomorrow to see what it is exactly he has done.

"I don't know how it happened, and what the injury is at the moment, so we'll have to wait and see tomorrow."

Who was 'a consistent threat'? Newcastle v Arsenal player ratings

Arsenal go six clear after lively draw at Newcastle

Arsenal are about to enter a gruelling period of games - with or without Raya.

In the next four weeks, they face Borussia Dortmund, Manchester City, Brentford, Tottenham Hotspur and Real Madrid.

"The one player that Arsenal cannot afford to lose is David Raya," said former England forward Alan Shearer, who is a pundit on Saturday's BBC Match of the Day. "He has made such a difference since joining from Brentford in 2023.

"They have top-class cover in just about every other position but he is the one individual that Mikel Arteta will be thinking 'we don't want to play without him for an extended period'. They could, of course go into the transfer market if they need to in January, but Arteta will be desperately hoping Raya is not out for long."

Raya is reportedly close to agreeing a new deal at the club, which shows his importance to the Gunners with two years remaining on his contract.

Ex-England midfielder Jamie Redknapp said on Sky Sports that Raya is "irreplaceable".

"Kepa is not up to the level of him - I actually think he struggles in the Premier League," added Redknapp. "Obviously we've seen in the Carabao Cup last year in the final.

"He is now going to have to play some games and that's going to be difficult for him.

"It will change everything for Arsenal for a while so that's a massive blow depending on how long David Raya is out because he is irreplaceable - probably the best goalkeeper in the Premier League, if not one of the best in the world."

#899. These gaps in weather data affect forecasts everywhere: plugging them is not charity

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Markus Repnik is a director at the Systematic Observations Financing Facility Secretariat in Geneva, Switzerland.

Observations from data-scarce regions, such as low-lying island Tuvalu in the South Pacific, are crucial to weather forecasts, early warning systems and climate-information services elsewhere. Credit: Mario Tama/Getty

When I talk about collecting essential weather and climate data in countries with limited resources, many take it to mean that wealthier countries, institutions and firms should ‘help poorer ones’. But as a development and climate-finance executive, I know that this is an investment rather than an act of charity. Science proves it: better forecasts at home rely on observations abroad.

That’s the resounding conclusion of a report published this month by The European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) in collaboration with the World Meteorological Organization (WMO). The report was commissioned by the Systematic Observations Financing Facility (SOFF), a United Nations fund dedicated to basic weather and climate data around the world, of which I am a director.

Its aim was to establish the benefits of filling gaps in the WMO’s Global Basic Observing Network (GBON), which defines member nations’ mandatory weather-station coverage. To comply, each country must have a land station every 200 kilometres, as well as a weather balloon every 500 kilometres over land and every 1,000 kilometres over sea to collect data on essential variables (such as temperature, pressure, humidity and wind).

Global climate body fights for survival: why the IPCC must be saved

Global climate body fights for survival: why the IPCC must be saved

But agreeing on standards and sites is not the same as having the economic means to implement them. Since 2023, GBON stations have been required to share their data. Yet, about 90% of weather data from low-income countries and small island nations are not being shared. Some data are not even collected because many stations are missing, stopped working or cannot transmit their measurements.

These gaps don’t just impede local forecasts, they affect regional and global projections too. Daily weather data feed into increasingly sophisticated computer models that predict how weather systems around the world evolve.

Think of a weather forecast as a photograph. It is made up of millions of pixels, each contributing a small piece of information. Weather forecasting is more complex, but the analogy helps to explain the problem: if too many ‘pixels’ are missing, the global picture is blurry or incomplete. And for forecasts, some ‘pixels’, or observations, are more valuable than others. Plugging gaps in data-scarce regions is the best way to improve forecasts everywhere.

It is also a matter of justice: on average, a seven-day temperature forecast in a high-income country is as accurate as a one-day forecast in a low-income country (M. Linsenmeier and J. G. Shrader Nature Commun. 17, 10792; 2026).

The results of the ECMWF simulations are striking. Better coverage in low-income countries and small island states can cut uncertainty in 12-hour local forecasts by more than 30% in parts of Africa and by up to 20% across the Pacific.

Extra data in all countries eligible for development assistance and small island nations would improve the accuracy of temperature and wind forecasts up to six or seven days ahead in the tropics, home to some 40% of the world’s population, and in the Northern Hemisphere’s mid-latitudes, where much of Europe, North America and northern Asia sit. This would help with, for example, aviation and maritime operations, planning of agricultural activities, water management and preparations for severe weather.

Disparity in countries’ capacity to finance weather observations is striking. To quantify the inequality, SOFF developed an indicator comparing countries’ gross dom-estic product (GDP) with the geographical area for which they are mandated to provide observations, including marine exclusive economic zones. For example, although it is a small country, Switzerland has a larger budget than does Tuvalu, a Pacific island nation spread across an immense ocean area (Switzerland’s GDP is around 300,000 times larger per square kilometre). Yet both countries contribute to and benefit from the same global observing system.

#898. Bruno Fernandes reveals talks over new Manchester United contract are on hold

Club captain confirms he has been offered a new deal

‘Not the right moment to be talking about negotiations’

Bruno Fernandes has revealed that Manchester United have offered him a new contract, but discussions have been ⁠put on hold as the club focus on turning around their terrible start to the season.

Fernandes’s current deal expires at the end of this campaign, although United ⁠hold an ​option to extend their captain’s contract by a further year until June 2028, giving the club more time to reach ⁠an agreement on fresh terms.

“The club offered me a new contract so I think that, from their side, shows that they ⁠want me to stay. And as you said, there are no negotiations going on,” ​Fernandes told Sky Sports in an ‌interview published on Sunday.

“We ‌spoke about the contract at the end of last season, we came in at ‌the beginning of this season speaking about the contract, but because of the context of the team and the club, I just put that to one side because I don’t think it’s the right moment, neither for me nor for the club, to be talking about negotiations,” Fernandes added. “The most important thing now is that ‌the club gets back to winning games.“

The 32-year-old’s future is still up in the air after it was revealed he turned down a second contract offer from the club. Fernandes’s form has dropped off this season, his goal and assist in the 4-4 draw against Aston Villa providing his first goal involvements in the league since scoring a hat-trick against Ipswich in August.

The Portugal international also hit back at rumours he had demanded more money and a longer deal, ​saying his priority was to remain at Old Trafford and help restore the club’s fortunes.

“I’ve ⁠seen people saying that he’s asked for more money, he’s asked ​for more years. If ​I wanted more money, I wouldn’t ​be here. I had somewhere to go to get much more ​money than being ‌at Manchester United,” ​Fernandes said. “I could ​have been in a place that’s much warmer than Manchester.”
