#861. Holders Celtic win 17-0 in Women's Scottish Cup

Isabella Fisher scored four goals in Celtic's win

Holders Celtic breezed through to the fourth round of the Women's Scottish Cup with a 17-0 victory over Forfar Farmington.

Morgan Cross and Casey Howe both netted hat-tricks, Isabella Fisher scored four times and Amy Gallacher bagged a double.

Lauren Doran-Barr, Addie Handley, Maria McAneny and Evie Rabjohn also scored and Forfar conceded an own goal.

Last season's beaten finalists, Rangers, were 5-0 victors at home to Motherwell.

Mijke Roelfsema opened the scoring with her first Rangers goal, Eilidh Austin made it two and Laura Berry converted a penalty shortly before going off injured.

Fallon Connolly-Jackson got her maiden Rangers goal early in the second half and Hannah Blake completed the scoring.

Glasgow City defeated Cambusdoon 10-0. Leah Lane scored her first City goal, with Kelly Brady, Lisa Forrest, Abi Harrison, Yuuka Kurosaki, Jesi Rossman and Emily Whelan also on target.

Sofia Maatta netted twice and Cambusdoon conceded an own goal.

Reigning Scottish champions Heart of Midlothian won 6-0 away to Stenhousemuir.

Lucy Jane Hope put the visitors in front and Jenny Smith doubled their lead. Ava Crawford got the third, Monica Forsyth also netted and Hope and Forsyth added to the tally.

Montrose won 13-0 at Dunipace, with Neve Guthrie, Kaela McDonald-Nguah and Hannah Stewart each scoring once, Francesca Ogilvie netting twice, Darcie Miller bagging a hat-trick and Demi Taylor picking up a four-goal haul, with an own goal also aiding the visitors.

Spartans were 11-2 winners at home to Bonnyrigg Rose. Zara Andrews and Ronaigh Douglas both scored once, there were doubles for Emily Cadell, Tegan Reynolds and Izzy Young, while Emma McMurdo scored a hat-trick.

Mya Christie, Holly Daniel, Christie again and Briana Salvetti all netted in Aberdeen's 4-0 home win over Dryburgh Athletic.

SWPL2 side Boroughmuir Thistle won 2-1 on penalties against top-flight Partick Thistle after a 1-1 draw. Imogen Longcake gave the visitors a second-half lead, but Amy Denholm levelled to force extra time.

Falkirk were 7-0 winners at home to Renfrew. Maisy Stewart, Skye Neillie, Mhari Smith, Caitlin McFarlane and Olivia Murphy all scored first-half goals, with McFarlane and Emma Lawson adding to the rout after the break.

Queen's Park beat Dundee United 2-1, with Ellie Kane and Darcy Molloy putting the hosts two up at the break and Lucy Stevenson replying in the second half.

Rossvale won 3-2 at home to Gartcairn. Maddie Wilson and Sarah Petherick had Rossvale 2-0 up, but Clare Docherty replied for the visitors before the break. Petherick's second proved to be the winner, with Gartcairn's Madison Maxwell netting a late consolation.

Livingston v Hamilton Academical was abandoned at half-time with Hamilton a goal up, while Inverurie Loco Works v Bishopton, Kilmarnock v Hibernian and Westdyke v St Johnstone were postponed.

#860. Champion’s corner: KC Current win first NWSL Championship with 2-1 stunner over Spirit

Current’s opener came direct from a corner kick

Debinha, Trinity Rodman trade goals in stoppage time

Washington Spirit lose third consecutive NWSL final

Read Jeff Rueter’s minute-by-minute report

It took five years, 90 minutes and a goal for the ages, but the Kansas City Current have their first-ever NWSL championship.

Riding a wave of momentum created by a 54th-minute Olimpico from midfielder Vanessa DiBernardo, and capping it off with an all-important breakaway winner from Debinha, the Current silenced the partisan, sellout crowd at the heavily-favored Washington Spirit’s home ground with a 2-1 victory on Saturday.

The Spirit, heartbroken at the final whistle, have now lost three consecutive NWSL Championships.

“Obviously this one hurts way worse than any of the other ones,” forward Trinity Rodman said afterward. “I don’t even think you have words in this moment — it is too fresh.”

DiBernardo’s goal was stunning, a driven, bent corner kick played to the far post that eluded Spirit goalkeeper Sandy MacIver, her defenders and Current forward Haley Hopkins, potentially DiBernardo’s intended target. The Spirit’s players and fans alike pleaded with center referee Joshua Encarnación, suggesting he examine the play on VAR for obstruction, as MacIver had potentially been screened. The review never came.

Whether played directly on goal intentionally or otherwise, the effort will go down as one of the most memorable in NWSL Championship history. At 34, DiBernardo becomes the oldest player in league history to score in a final, and was later named the match’s MVP.

“I’ve been to the game a few times and haven’t won, but this one just felt a little lighter,” said DiBernardo, who gave birth to Charlie, her first child, in January and took time off before returning to the Current in March. “I think just having Charlie, it just brings a different perspective on life. I knew the game was big and it was a big moment, but just kinda having her, just spending the day with her, it just felt really special.”

The game’s early phases were forgettable save for one incident which would go on to affect the remainder of the match: a bruising, high-speed tackle on Rodman by Current defender Laney Rouse in the fifth minute. The challenge sent Rodman flying and appeared to injure her left elbow; the Spirit forward, nearing tears, spent much of the first half in visible pain and seemingly never fully recovered. Rouse was not cautioned for the challenge.

“[It helped set the tone] in the sense that it hurt really bad, yes,” Rodman said. “As a team, you always want to put the first hit in. You’re taught to do that. Credit to them. I wish I was the one who put her on the ground. They did a really good job at setting the tone and controlling the first half.”

It was far from the game’s only physical moment. Neither team managed to settle into any meaningful rhythm during an opening 45 that felt at times more like a title fight than a title match. Encarnación, involved in his first NWSL final, called a very tight match and the near-constant stoppages in play were the defining characteristic of a sometimes ugly opening phase. In many ways it was not entirely his fault: the message-sending start from KC and the Spirit’s subsequent response often compelled him to act. The 19 combined first-half fouls between both sides were the most in any half of any NWSL title match in league history.

“It felt like we couldn’t play more than two minutes without a whistle,” Rodman said. “We were fouling, they were true calls for sure — but I think you lose control of the game really quickly that way ... It definitely messed with our rhythm a little bit.”

Paradoxically, though, the match was won with speed. Deep into second-half stoppage time, the Current found their eventual match-winner on a breakaway. After doggedly winning back possession after a Spirit free kick late on, Kansas City forward Debinha streaked upfield from just beyond the center stripe, looking off a wide-open Temwa Chawinga and rounding MacIver who looked on hopelessly as the Brazilian slotted it home.

No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football

Moments later, Rodman – somehow still in the match after not only the early challenge but a later high-speed collision with Current goalkeeper Lorena – pulled one back for the Spirit. Falling away from goal 10 yards out, Rodman got her head on the end of a Tara Rudd cross, placing it perfectly over Lorena’s outstretched arms and into the far-side netting. The ensuing five minutes – the game ended in the 102nd – were chaotic but the Spirit couldn’t quite find the equalizer.

After a slow start, the Current were well-managed by former Major League Soccer and US national team member Chris Armas. Armas was widely considered a controversial selection at the time of his appointment but proceeded to lead the club to their first championship in his first season, doing so by beating Gotham FC and now the Spirit, two sides picked by many as potential league-winners.

“I think from the front to the back we made it a point that every person on this team defends and if somebody is going to make a mistake the other person is going to have their back,” Current defender Izzy Rodriguez said. “We try and turn every 1v1 situation into a 1v2 for us, and I think that showed up today. We were winning our duels and second balls and those are things that win games.”

For the Spirit, the loss is devastating. They become the first American professional club – men’s or women’s – to lose three consecutive finals since the New England Revolution of Major League Soccer, who did so in the mid 2000s. In their five Championship appearances, the Spirit have won just one time, in 2021.

#859. Watford seek sixth manager in 18 months after sacking Dionisi

Alessio Dionisi was the fifth Italian manager hired by Watford under the ownership of the Pozzo family

Watford are looking for their sixth manager in 18 months after they sacked head coach Alessio Dionisi following 18 games in charge.

The 46-year-old Italian was appointed in June after the departure of Ed Still, who himself lasted only three months at Vicarage Road.

Still, Javi Gracia and Paulo Pezzolano were all also given full-time contracts after Tom Cleverley left in May 2025.

Dionisi was Watford's 12th head coach, not including interim bosses, since the end of the 2020-21 season, and leaves the Hornets searching for a 25th since the Pozzo family took over the club in 2012.

The club have had 57 permanent managers in their 145-year history.

The decision to replace him comes after Saturday's crushing 4-0 defeat by Sheffield United at Bramall Lane.

Dionisi's dismissal caps an underwhelming start to the season, with the Hornets having won just four league games to leave them 21st in the table.

"We thank Alessio and his staff for his professionalism and their efforts," sporting director Luke Dowling told the club website., external

"As I'm sure the supporters have seen, Alessio is a really good guy and we wish him the best for the future.

"The process has started for a replacement and we hope to be in a position to announce that shortly."

Dionisi was sacked by Serie B club Empoli in March after only five months in charge following a run of five wins in 22 matches.

His spell in charge of the Hornets was his first outside his homeland and started promisingly when his youthful side beat Southampton in their opening league game.

But they won only two of their next 12 in all competitions, and despite deservedly beating Charlton on 17 October, reverses at Wolves and Norwich followed, before four points from Dionisi's final three games in charge of the Hertfordshire side and his dismissal means further upheaval for the Hornets.

With more than a third of the league season complete, Watford are one place outside of the Championship relegation zone (table shown before Burnley face Blackburn on Sunday)

Since sacking Cleverley at the end of the 2024-25 campaign, the club has now been through four permanent head coaches, as well as interim boss Charlie Daniels' two-game spell in charge.

Of those four, only Gracia, in his second spell at Vicarage Road, took charge of more than 20 games.

On the morning of their final-day drubbing by Coventry last season, chief executive Scott Duxbury wrote a statement on the club website saying Watford had made mistakes, labelling their end to the campaign "unacceptable" and "truly disappointing in the extreme".

#858. Borussia Dortmund's Felix Nmecha and the question of religion

Felix Nmecha's "Crowns down" celebration has drawn criticism from a Borussia Dortmund fan club, reopening debate over faith, inclusion and religious messaging in football.

Felix Nmecha's renewed use of the "Crowns down celebration" — where a crown is pretended to be removed from someone's head and placed at Jesus' feet — has sparked a reaction from Borussia Dortmund's official supporters' group.

"Faith does not justify exclusion. Faith does not justify division. Borussia Dortmund is a club for everyone," read a statement after the Bundesliga club beat Elversberg, a game in which Nmecha scored twice. Nmecha's first documented "Crowns down celebration" was at the 2026 World Cup, for which "The King's Return" campaign was launched.

"In the past, the the Borussia Dortmund supporters club has deliberately refrained from commenting on sports-related issues and the athletic performance of individual players. We remain committed to this approach," the statement continued.

"However, when it comes to our club's values, discrimination, and the question of what view of humanity is fostered within and around Borussia Dortmund, we cannot and will not remain silent."

The fan club states their issue is not with Nmecha being a devout Christian, but rather his public support for "The King's Return" campaign, which the supporters club said "gives us cause to reassess the situation."

This campaign, according to research by German public broadcaster ARD in the summer of 2026, was designed by the "Ballers in God" (BIG) network. BIG was founded in 2015 by footballer John Bostock, a devout Christian who wanted to create a community where professional footballers could strengthen each other in their faith, pray together, and read the Bible. In over a decade since, the BIG community has grown to nearly 800,000 followers on Instagram.

Nmecha issued a response on social media not long afterwards, writing:

"I've been told that my most recent goal celebration has led to some misunderstandings," Nmecha wrote.

"My message was never intended to spread intolerance, discrimination, or hatred in any form. As Christians, our message is one of love and respect for every person—regardless of where someone comes from, what they believe in, or what worldview they hold."

Reports suggest that both the board at Dortmund and Germany head coach Jürgen Klopp will speak to Nmecha on the matter in the coming days.

The fan club say their criticism is "directed at religious networks that, under the guise of faith, promote a worldview in which people are devalued or marginalized because of their sexual orientation, gender identity, lifestyle, or personal choices... When religious beliefs are used to deny people their dignity or equality, that is where our tolerance for intolerance ends."

Here, they are referring to the recent ARD investigation. That work revealed the homepage for "The King's Return" campaign featured a link to a live counseling chat run by US-based evangelical nonprofit Groundwire. During the investigations, counselors told reporters that abortion is "Satan's plan" and that homosexuality is a sin.

Borussia Dortmund's statement of core values commits the club to diversity, human rights, and inclusion regardless of gender, sexual orientation, faith, or background. The club's largest and most influential fan group also promotes progressive, anti-fascist, and inclusive values. It is also part of a wider fan landscape in Germany where club members are more involved in club decisions than in many other countries. This was evidenced when the club signed a deal with arms manufacturer Rheinmetall two years ago and in the case of Nmecha as well. When the midfielder signed for Dortmund in 2023, many of the club's fans protested because the player had previously shared or liked several transphobic and homophobic posts on his Instagram account. In response, Nmecha deleted some posts and instead issued a statement emphasizing "I do not discriminate against anyone."

Article 4 of German Basic Law guarantees that each individual is allowed to decide how strongly, why and which god to believe in. In football, players cannot display political, religious, or personal slogans, statements, or images on their jerseys, undershirts, or gear. However, physical gestures are allowed so long as they don't delay the game or antagonize the crowd.

The use of physical religious gestures has history in sports, as professor Paul Putz described in his book "The Spirit of the Game: American Christianity and Big-Time Sports". Putz describes how the the pioneers of the Christian athlete movement realized they: "could influence others to Christian ideals more effectively on the field than in the pulpit."

And yet, such gestures can also be at odds with the atmosphere of modern sports arenas, particularly football. In their book "Sports and Christianity: Historical and Contemporary Perspectives", Nick J. Watson and Andrew Parker explain how modern sport has become a substitute for traditional faith.

"Sport seduces the teeming 'global village'; it is the new opiate of the masses; it is one of the great modern experiences … Sport, for many, has replaced religion as a source of emotional catharsis and spiritual passion," they wrote.

With the 26-year-old Nmecha a key player for both club and country, the conversation around faith and football looks set to continue for some time yet.

#857. ‘Obviously it’s not good’: Arteta sweating over David Raya’s fitness after injury

Keeper close to tears at Newcastle after hurting shoulder

Arsenal held 2-2, with Jaissle hailing ‘excellent’ display

Arsenal were left sweating on the fitness of their goalkeeper David Raya after the Spaniard was forced off with a shoulder injury during the second half of the 2-2 draw at Newcastle on Saturday evening.

It left Mikel Arteta’s side six points clear of Brighton and Manchester City at the top of the Premier League but Arsenal’s manager was more concerned about Raya following an accidental collision with Newcastle’s William Osula. The Spaniard was helped off in evident pain and looked close to tears.

“Obviously it’s not good David had to come off but at the moment I don’t know [the prognosis],” said Arteta, explaining that a keeper who kept seven clean sheets in the season’s opening 10 games will have the joint scanned on Sunday. “He will have an MRI tomorrow. We will have more information tomorrow. But we know how important David is to us.”

Arsenal were 1-0 up at half-time at St James’ Park thanks to a goal from Eberechi Eze during an opening 45 minutes dominated by the visitors. Newcastle, though, improved significantly after the break and took the lead thanks to goals from Harvey Barnes and Malick Thiaw before Noni Madueke equalised.

In the Guardian app, tap the Profile settings button at the top right, then select Notifications. Turn on sport notifications.

If you don't have the Guardian app, download it from the iOS App Store on iPhone or the Google Play store on Android by searching for 'The Guardian'.

“My feeling is we have lost two points,” said Arteta. “We were exceptional in the first half but we needed to score three or four goals and we didn’t. We knew there’d be a response but the way we gave Newcastle’s first goal away was completely unacceptable. We came back and scored a second goal but we lacked the moment of magic to kill the game. I don’t think we switched off in the second half; sometimes you have to praise the opposition.”

Matthias Jaissle was left smiling after that second-half performance rescued a game watched by Newcastle’s chair, Yasir al-Rumayyan. He had flown in from Riyadh to witness his first match of the season and is believed to have complimented his head coach afterwards.

“What you saw in the second half was Newcastle’s DNA par excellence and that’s something we can build on,” said Jaissle. “But we’ve got to be humble and realistic. The first half was not good and the second half was excellent. I’ve got mixed feelings because a little more was possible but a point was probably fair.

“I was a bit frustrated at half-time but we encouraged the players to do the high press in the right way and adopt a front-foot approach. There was no hesitating, no doubting, just pure belief and we clicked. I knew we were able to do it, so I was really pleased. We felt unbelievable connections and synergy with the crowd.

“To get a team as good as Arsenal shaking in your stadium was unbelievable. I hope we can carry on this feeling.”

#856. DWTS’ Sharna Burgess Slams Fans for Using Voting to "Manipulate" Show

Dancing With the Stars pro Sharna Burgess accused fans of using the voting system to “vote people off” and “manipulate the show” following Harry Shum Jr. and Jenna Johnson’s Nov. 17 elimination.

Sharna Burgess believes Dancing With the Stars fans took a wrong turn with the latest elimination.

Days after frontrunners Harry Shum Jr. and Jenna Johnson were sent home during the show's semifinals Nov. 17, the DWTS pro detailed her theory behind their exit, accusing viewers of using the voting system to eliminate contestants they don’t like rather than supporting their favorites.

“Sadly no, I felt it was going to be another shock elimination,” Burgess wrote on her Instagram Stories Nov. 20, replying to a fan who asked if she was surprised Shum and Johnson were sent home. “Not because they deserved it but simply because the online discourse is so wild that [it] was pretty clear who fans were ‘voting off’ and how they have felt about dance experience contestants.”

But according to the 41-year-old—who was paired with Bachelor Nation’s Tyler Cameron for season 35 before their Oct. 27 elimination—the issue is much bigger than a single misstep.

“[It’s] so disappointing to see our voting system is now being used by viewers to vote people off instead of voting for your favorite,” Burgess continued, before pointing to how fans can cast 20 votes per couple. “I say we got [sic] back to yall only have 10 votes total and you have to figure out how to dish them out.”

As the professional dancer put it, “This voting ppl off thing is so insanely negative and not what we are built on and it's seemingly given fans the chance to manipulate the show. JMO.”

On the Nov. 17 episode, Shum, 44, and Johnson, 32, were eliminated despite receiving perfect scores on both of their dances. This marked the second week in a row a frontrunner pair—which also featured a celebrity with previous dance experience—was sent home, as Johnson’s husband Val Chmerkovskiy and his partner Jenna Dewan were voted off the week prior.

As for the Grey’s Anatomy star’s thoughts on his elimination?

“I oddly feel at ease. I don't feel sad—it's really weird,” Shum told E! News in an interview after his elimination. “I kind of felt like we accomplished everything we wanted to.”

As Dancing With the Stars spins into the season 35 finale, keep reading for a closer look at the show’s secrets…

How Much Do the Celebrities Get Paid to Be on Dancing With the Stars?

Citing multiple sources, Variety reported in 2019 that Dancing With the Stars contestants make $125,000 for the rehearsal period and first two weeks of the show. If they progress beyond that point, the outlet continued, they earn more money each week. At the time, sources told the publication stars could earn a maximum of $295,000.

However, Bobby Bones said he made more than this when he won season 27 with Sharna Burgess in 2018.

"That show pays OK," the radio personality said on a Sept. 2025 episode of Jason Tartick's podcast Trading Secrets. "Like, first episode, no money. Second episode, $10,000. I think it's like, $10,000, $10,000, $20,000, $20,000. It ends up being $50,000 an episode if you last."

Also receiving a base salary of around $110,000, Bones continued, "I ended up making close to $400,000 from that show."

ABC has not publicly confirmed any of these figures.

What Do the Pros Get Paid on Dancing With the Stars?

Similarly, little has been shared publicly about how much the pros get paid. But as with the contestants, it seems like the longer they're on the show, the more money they can make.

But even if a pro is eliminated in the first round, they're not leaving the ballroom empty-handed.

"You're guaranteed until a certain amount of weeks," Jenna Johnson said on a June 2025 episode of Kelly Stafford and Hank Winchester's podcast The Morning After. "I think there's different contracts though. I can't speak for everybody."

Do Pros Get Paid More If They Win Dancing With the Stars?

While Johnson—who won season 26 with Olympic figure skater Adam Rippon, as well as season 33 with The Bachelor's Joey Graziadei—says the pros don't get a larger paycheck if they take home what is now called the Len Goodman Mirrorball Trophy, she noted there's still an incentive to make it to the finale (besides bragging rights, of course).

"If you make it all the way to the end, you're getting paid the whole season, which is amazing, and you get a bonus on top of that for making it to the finale," she explained on The Morning After. "If you win, it's not like you win a $1 million and split it with your partner. You're just getting a cute trophy together."

Do the Troupe Members Get Paid as Much as the Pros on Dancing With the Stars?

On a 2022 episode of Trading Secrets, Lindsay Arnold recalled how her salary was cut "more than in half" when she was demoted from pro to troupe member.

How Are Pros and Celebrities Paired Together on Dancing With the Stars?

The pros get little input when it comes to being matched with a celebrity.

"You get no say," Lindsay said on a May 2025 episode of Maggie Sellers' Hot Smart Rich podcast. "It's very much just, 'Here's your partner. Make it work.'"

In fact, Jenna said the pairing is often a secret until the last minute.

"They really want to keep it a secret until you meet them live," Jenna said on The Morning After. "They want that genuine reaction. So I think people always think we know who we have and we're keeping it a secret. Absolutely not. They do not tell us. They really don't even want us to know the cast. It gets leaked a lot, but they want it very hush-hush until you walk in and meet your partner."

As for what the Dancing With the Stars team looks for when making these matches?

"It's based on height, build and personality and compatibility," former showrunner Rob Wade told E! News in 2015. "We don't pair people who aren't going to get on. It's too intense. It's not like The Bachelor or something, we couldn't do that. That would just be miserable experience for the celebrity, for us and the viewer. You don't want to see two people who don't like each other and, quite frankly, we have made that mistake pairing people up who didn't get on so well."

How Often Do the Pros and Celebrities Practice on Dancing With the Stars?

Put simply, a lot."Every day we have four-hour rehearsals," Rylee Arnold, who was partnered with Olympic gymnast Stephen Nedoroscik on season 33, shared on a September 2024 episode of the Lightweights Podcast With Joe Vulpis. "It’s either 9:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m., 1:00 p.m. to 5:00 p.m. or 5:00 p.m to 9:00 p.m."But the work doesn't stop once the rehearsal wraps. Rylee noted she might then meet with producers or the creative team, work on choreography or study dance videos."Literally my whole life is devoted to it," she continued, "but it's my passion and it's what I love. So, it makes me so happy."Indeed, it's a no-days-off kind of gig."We have our show day on Tuesday and then it's Wednesday to Sunday, straight rehearsals," Rylee added. "And then Monday we have camera blocking and then Tuesday's show day again."

Do the Pros Get to Pick the Songs Each Week for Their Dance With Their Celebrity Partner?

"Mostly yes," Emma Slater and Britt Stewart revealed in a September 2025 Instagram video, "though it's a collaboration with producers."

What's the Process Like for Making the Costumes for Dancing With the Stars?

If you thought the quickstep was fast, just wait until you hear about the pace of the costume department."We meet with the set and lighting designers, dancers and talent and create a story [for each pair]," costume designer Daniela Gschwendtner told TV Insider back in 2017. "Then we sketch out ideas. We have five days, max, to make all the outfits. That’s half a day per costume, not including all the rhinestones. The fitting and trimming we do later. We have about 20 people in our department and then we have a separate tailor shop. It’s a big enterprise."In fact, costume designer Steven Norman Lee said pairs usually try on their costumes for the first time just hours before showtime. And while the department "might use a pair of pants again for the boys," he continued, everything is generally made custom each week.As Gschwendtner added, "We do reuse things for group numbers or promo shoots, but not for the competition. We don’t reuse things unless there’s a specific reason to do so. We try to keep everybody fresh and new in something different every week, so it stays interesting."

#854. Claude, find me a planet: amateur astronomers are using AI with mixed results

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Artificial-intelligence tools are helping citizen scientists to find undiscovered exoplanets (artist’s illustration).Credit: Hypersphere/SPL

In September, Pavel Rabtsevich sat down at his computer and asked an AI model to discover a planet. Rabtsevich directed the program to a specific batch of telescope data and gave it a high-level plan to hunt for evidence of undetected planets. In about two weeks, the program delivered the goods: two possible planets orbiting a star 116 light years from Earth. Professional astronomers are now checking the findings.

History’s long-secret codes are being cracked by amateurs using AI

History’s long-secret codes are being cracked by amateurs using AI

Rabtsevich, who works in Spain as an artificial-intelligence specialist and has no formal astronomy education, is one of the most successful of a wave of amateur astronomers who are using AI models to search for worlds outside the Solar System. Citizen scientists have been using publicly available tools from NASA and other researchers to find planets for decades. But AI’s ability to scour the Internet for such tools and use them to process massive amounts of data has lowered the barrier to entry for non-specialists who want to become planet hunters.

The newfound accessibility of data-analysis tools, however, has meant that not all amateurs are doing research responsibly, says Michelle Kunimoto, an exoplanet researcher at the University of British Columbia in Vancouver, Canada. Some planet hunters don’t fully understand the algorithms being used by AI tools and thus can’t validate the models’ findings, Kunimoto says. “There’s been a huge, overwhelming surge of AI-driven papers, which tend to have [planet] candidates that are not the best quality,” they say. And as a result, “the systems we use to disseminate science are being overwhelmed”.

For his search, Rabtsevich enlisted Claude Code, an AI coding tool made by Anthropic. He asked it to sift through data from more than 120,000 stars observed by NASA’s Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) in late 2025 and early 2026. He guided Claude to use a popular planet-detection algorithm to search for dips in the stars’ brightness. A regular and repeated dimming of a star can be a sign that a planet is orbiting it and blocking a little bit of light every time it passes between the star and an observer.

Claude zeroed in on a star called TIC 4206066, which showed two separate cycles of dimming, one roughly every 3 days and another every 11 days. That suggests that TIC 4206066 is orbited by two planets, one of which loops around the star more tightly than the other and thus takes less time to complete a full rotation.

These alien planets are astronomers’ favourites

These alien planets are astronomers’ favourites

Rabtsevich instructed Claude to look for those same repetitive patterns in archival TESS data. Sure enough, data from 2018 and 2020 recorded the same pattern of dimming coming from TIC 4206066. At Rabtsevich’s direction, Claude then found a planet-detection algorithm, one written and made publicly available by Kunimoto, and ran it to validate the signals.

Rabtsevich published his findings to the platform Zenodo as a preprint1 on 25 September. His work has not been peer reviewed, but TESS astronomers have completed an independent analysis of the signals and have added them to their official list of planet candidates.

#853. Robins ‘aims for the stars’ as Stoke dream of Premier League return

The Championship’s form side climbed to second after holding on resiliently with 10 men to knock Birmingham off the summit

There have been false dawns before. Plenty of them. This time last year, with Christmas on the near horizon, Stoke sat second in the Championship table and were beginning to wonder whether they might allow themselves to dream. So hopeless was their subsequent run that by the onset of spring they were forced to consider a potential relegation fight.

Experience has taught the benefit of pragmatism, so no one will be getting ahead of themselves just yet. But this weekend was supposed to be the big test for Mark Robins’s team and few considered they would pass it quite so resoundingly.

Facing a Birmingham side who arrived top of the table and with firmly held Premier League ambitions, Stoke dominated for an hour, the hitherto goal-shy George Hirst earning a well-deserved lead to send a bumper crowd into raptures. The hand-wringing that then followed Luca Bombino’s sending-off with half an hour remaining made the victory that followed all the sweeter. The 10 men of Stoke were superb. It was no surprise that it took considerable time to convince those in the stands to depart for home after the final whistle.

You see, it is not just that Stoke are second in the table, kept off top spot by goal difference. It is not even that they are undoubtedly the Championship’s form side, with just one defeat in their past 13 games. It is the whole feeling around the place; the resilience Robins has developed, and the belief that they can take on the big guns and beat them.

“We are a work in progress, but today was that step in quality against different opponents. A step up in class,” said Robins. “I thought we were really, really good. The intensity, bravery and the intent that we showed was everything that we asked for.

“And, on the back of that, you’ve got the support that are absolutely right behind us. They trust the players. That is a really good feeling. It’s a great feeling for the players. It’s a heady mix, really.”

Eight years have passed since Stoke were last in the top flight; eight years spent as the Championship equivalent of a sea sponge, doing the bare minimum to survive and letting defeats wash over them while remaining resolutely attached to the rocks of the bottom half of the table. During that time they have ended every campaign no higher than 14th and no lower than 18th. Now, something altogether different is afoot. And this may well be the win that convinces supporters to trust their upbeat instincts.

There was an unavoidable fact heading into Saturday’s game. Stoke’s four defeats this season had all come when tasked with opponents fighting at the top end of the table in Swansea, Southampton, Wolves and Middlesbrough. They had shown themselves capable against much of the division, but a failure to deliver against another Championship heavyweight would have raised legitimate questions about their realistic aspirations.

The three August defeats at the start of the campaign preceded the departure of their best player, Sorba Thomas. His replacement, Jack McGlynn, has been an inspired signing. That this victory came without the talismanic figure of Ethan Galbraith, who was absent through illness, is considerable.

As well as switching to a three-man defence following those season-opening losses, a key factor in their upturn has been the restoration of a touch of old-school Stoke; a physicality that was frequently evident on a cold Saturday afternoon.

Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football

Bobby Madley, the referee, did not always take kindly to such an approach – to the indignation of the home crowd, who frequently made their feelings clear – but there was no complaint over Bombino’s sending-off for a second yellow after a rash challenge that left him head in hands before the card had even been shown. Tears followed on his slow trudge towards the tunnel, but he need not have worried, with Birmingham barely threatening thereafter.

Given just five points separate the top eight in the Championship table, it would come as no great shock to see Stoke drop off at some point. They do not have the financial benefit of recent Premier League parachute payments or big-spending owners, they are not prolific goalscorers, and a look at their expected goals and expected points tallies shows them firmly in the bottom half of the table. But they are finding ways to win and if McGlynn has a habit of scoring from unexpectedly long distances, perhaps it is because he is good at it.

Before this weekend, Robins had revealed that a top-eight finish was the pre-season target. “You aim for the stars and hopefully you land trying to grab hold of one,” he had said, rather poetically.

If promotion is a “P” they dare not yet speak of, another one – playoffs – is becoming an increasingly realistic proposition. No more sticking to a rock. Swim free and prosper.

#850. Blackburn earn derby draw for Mowbray and extend Burnley’s wait for home win

Todd Cantwell’s penalty earned Blackburn a 2-2 draw at Burnley in their first match since Tony Mowbray stepped back because of health issues.

In a gripping, physical East Lancashire derby, the home side led twice, through Largie Ramazani’s rising first-half drive and Jaydon Banel’s steered finish after the break. But Andri Gudjohnsen scored Blackburn’s first equaliser, then earned the penalty which Cantwell converted.

Burnley remain deep in relegation trouble, without a home league victory for 400 days, having once again failed to hold on to a lead. They have now dropped 25 points from winning positions in the Championship this season.

Blackburn wanted a victory not just for local pride, but to honour Mowbray, who turned 63 on Sunday, and for whom this was to be a 900th match in management before his announcement on Tuesday that he would be stepping back. Their players warmed up in T-shirts bearing the message “We’re with you, Tony” on the back and the number 900 on the front.

Coaches Damien Johnson and Mike Dodds have taken charge in Mowbray’s absence and had to reshuffle the defence when Tom Atcheson was concussed after receiving a boot to the face in the third minute.

The stand-in goalkeeper Aynsley Pears, playing after Balazs Toth sustained a broken hand on international duty with Hungary, pushed over a fierce deflected shot from Banel, but was at fault when Ramazani gave Burnley a 27th-minute lead.

The on-loan Leeds winger cut in from the right and fired a shot that flew into the roof of the net right by Pears, who was too slow to react.

But Gudjohnsen equalised four minutes later, racing on to a Harry Pickering long ball that drifted over Burnley centre-back Max Alleyne, and steering a sweet shot beyond goalkeeper Max Weiss for his 12th goal of the season. The Icelander celebrated by grabbing a Mowbray-tribute T-shirt from a photographer and displaying it for the cameras.

Blackburn finished the first half strongly, with Cantwell firing over a good chance, before Banel restored Burnley’s lead six minutes into the second half, running unchallenged to place a shot into the far corner as Hayden Carter backed off.

The home side were fortunate to escape a strong penalty appeal just before the hour mark as Cantwell burst into the penalty area and saw two attempted crosses both strike the arm of Igor Julio.

Blackburn did get a penalty with 16 minutes left as Josh Laurent, attempting to clear a low cross, failed to spot Gudjohnsen darting in from behind him and caught the striker’s leg. Cantwell drove the penalty straight down the middle to make it 2-2.

Gudjohnsen thought he had given Blackburn the lead two minutes later, when he controlled and drove a low shot against the base of the post with Weiss a spectator, but neither side could find a winner.

#848. McBurnie’s added-time double snatches win for Hull to shock 10-man Brighton

Amid the talk of Brighton being surprise title contenders this season, these are perhaps the afternoons which show the margin that still exists, and how the Premier League can provide the most punishing of wake-up calls at any moment.

Make no mistake about it, Fabian Hürzeler’s side will play far worse than this over the next few months and win. They are still second in the table. How they left Hull without even a point almost defies belief given the dominance they enjoyed for large parts of the contest. But for all the statement victories and the headline-grabbing moments, these games are the ones which can trip you up the most.

A blisteringly cold November afternoon in Hull, against a promoted side where the expectation for a team challenging for the title is to win, and perhaps win with minimum fuss, too. On another afternoon, Brighton may have done just that, were it not for the heroics of Hull’s goalkeeper, Konstantinos Tzolakis.

But the best teams, the ones that end the seasons lifting the silverware, almost always seem to find a way. Tzolakis was the Seagulls’ scourge with a string of sensational saves that kept Hull in a contest where, for large periods, they were struggling to keep their heads above water.

However, the goal Brighton deserved never arrived – and as this game wore on you wondered if a team like Hull, whose commitment can never be questioned and who are tough to beat on their own turf, could dig in for long enough to provide a sucker punch on the counter. That moment arrived, not perhaps with Oli McBurnie’s goal that broke the deadlock in stoppage time, but two minutes before.

When João Costinha was shown a second yellow card in the 89th minute for a foul on Sorba Thomas, the MKM Stadium responded. They sensed that Tzolakis’s heroics could perhaps produce more than just a point, with Brighton forced to sit in and try to hold out for the closing moments. Hull surged forward, with McBurnie bundling home from close to range to spark delirium among the home support.

Two minutes later, with Brighton now left pressing just to try to find an equaliser, Hull caught them cold and McBurnie would tap into an empty net to seal the most unlikely of victories for the Tigers, who remain unbeaten at home since promotion. This was their first win since August, however, and a welcome tonic to put breathing space between themselves and the bottom three.

“We played against an excellent team who play intensive football,” Hull’s manager, Sergej Jakirovic, said. “I wish this feeling would never stop because we’ve had to wait for this.” But this was an afternoon that was as much about Brighton as it was Hull.

A win here would have closed the gap to Arsenal at the top to three points. In the end, this was a huge missed opportunity, with Hürzeler understandably crestfallen post-match.

Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football

“In the Premier League you can never expect to win,” he said. “For us, it’s very important with our identity and every game you have to lift your standards. If you drop, the Premier League is too good and it will punish you.”

McBurnie may have been the hero but there was no doubting the star man was Tzolakis. He denied Brighton on so many occasions and otherwise the game could have been over before the interval. First, he denied Diego Gómez from close range before stopping Yasin Ayari’s effort.

Two minutes later, Georginio Rutter was the next to be denied by the Greece international with another smart save before the pick of the bunch: Tzolakis made a reaction save with his foot to turn Gómez’s effort wide after Brighton cut Hull open at will again. At that stage it felt like when, not if, the visitors went ahead. Nobody told Tzolakis that.

Half-time did little to change the flow of momentum. Pascal Gross was next to be denied by Tzolakis before Gómez then shot wide from six yards out. At the other end, Hull were showing signs of coming to life, with two Mohamed Belloumi breaks a warning sign of what was to follow for the visitors.

Tzolakis was finally beaten by Charalampos Kostoulas when his chipped effort beat his fellow countryman, but Regan Slater was on hand to clear off the line. Then, as time ebbed away, Costinha’s second yellow decisively swung the momentum and within two minutes, Hull scored the goal Brighton had craved.

First, McBurnie bundled home before Belloumi’s break led to him squaring for the Scotland international to tap into an empty net. Was it what Brighton deserved? Probably not. But try persuading anyone of a Hull persuasion to care about that.

#847. Stassi Schroeder Has Shady Reaction to Jax Taylor's Cancer Diagnosis

Stassi Schroeder shared her reaction to ex Jax Taylor’s cancer diagnosis in an exclusive interview with E! News during People and InStyle’s Drive-By Party in Las Vegas.

Stassi Schroeder makes it a rule not to comment on her ex Jax Taylor.

Days after the The Valley alum—who dated Schroeder from 2010-2013—shared he was diagnosed with kidney cancer, the Vanderpump Villa host revealed her reaction to his health news.

“One of confusion,” Schroeder exclusively told E! News at People and InStyle’s Drive-By Party at the Las Vegas Grand Prix Nov. 20. “I'm not here to doubt somebody's diagnosis. I hope the best for everyone involved.”

As for whether she has a message for Taylor, she simply noted, “no.”

But Schroeder—whose relationship with Taylor was chronicled during their time on Vanderpump Rules—isn’t on the outs with all of her former costars. After all, Katie Maloney accompanied the You Can’t Have It All author to the event.

“Well, Katie Maloney is here with me right now,” Schroeder noted, “so her.”

And while the 38-year-old—who shares kids Hartford, 5, and Messer, 3, with husband Beau Clark—may be tight-lipped about where she stands with her fellow reality stars, she’s also not interested in clearing up any rumors floating around about them.

“You know what, let's just let them all live,” she said. “Let's let them all go and let everyone run with them.”

Taylor, 47, shared he was diagnosed with cancer after a tumor was discovered on his kidney during treatment for kidney stones in July.

“This is something I’ve kept private for the past few months because it’s been one of the scariest times of my life,” he wrote in a Nov. 19 Instagram post, which featured photos from his hospital bed and a video of him walking with the help of a walker. “What I thought was just a kidney stone turned into something I never imagined. My CT scan also showed a tumor on my left kidney. After many tests and appointments I found out it was cancer.”

Taylor—who shares 5-year-old son Cruz with estranged wife Brittany Cartwright—shared that the diagnosis was especially challenging given his father had died of cancer. As he said of the moment he learned of his diagnosis, “It broke me.”

As a part of his treatment, the reality TV star underwent surgery in which a source close to Taylor exclusively told E! News Nov. 19 that he’d experienced "some complications.”

However, the source noted that through it all, Taylor has had his girlfriend Lori Krebs by his side.

"The last few months have really taken a toll on him and she’s always been someone who brings him a sense of peace,” the source said. “They’ve been through a lot together and there’s a very deep love and connection between them."

The insider added, "They’re truly there for one another, and I think going through something like this has only made them realize just how much they mean to each other."

Keep reading for closer look into the love lives of more Vanderpump Rules stars…

Much of Vanderpump Rules' first season, which debuted in 2013, focused on the drama surrounding Jax Taylor cheating on then-girlfriend Stassi Schroeder in Las Vegas. And after his hook-up with co-star Kristen Doute was revealed during season two, the couple broke up for good.

The VPR alum began dating the casting executive in 2017 while she was still on the show. After she was fired from the series in 2020, Schroeder and Beau Clark legally tied the knot in September of that year during the COVID-19 pandemic before welcoming daughter Hartford in January 2021.

The two later held a formal wedding in Italy in May 2022 and welcomed their second child, son Messer, in 2023.

Jax Taylor & Brittany Cartwright: Separated

Taylor and Brittany Cartwright met during a 2015 trip to Vegas following his breakup from Schroeder. After surviving a cheating scandal involving Taylor and their former co-star Faith Stowers, he and Cartwright wed in 2019 at a castle in her native Kentucky. Their wedding special aired on Bravo shortly after.

The pair welcomed their son Cruz in April 2021, a year after they walked away from the show.

Six months after they announced their separation in February 2024 (and Taylor's subsequent trips to rehab), she officially filed for divorce.

Following his breakup from longtime girlfriend Doute, Sandoval and fellow bartender Ariana Madix began dating when she joined the show during the third season in 2013. The duo proved to be one of VPR's most dependable couples for nine years as they bought a house, adopted dogs and even wrote a cocktail book together.

Because of their stability, fans were shocked when the TomTom co-owner's seven-month affair with their co-star Rachel "Raquel" Leviss came to light in March 2023, leading to his and Madix's breakup.

"I think when you know, you know," the Love Island host explained to E! News in 2025 of finding her person (and personal trainer), "and I think very early on I was just like, 'There's something different about this guy.' He continues to show up for me, like, consistently."

Two years after her 2017 divorce from ex Mike Shay, SURver Scheana Shay met Brock Davies while out with friends in San Diego and it was love at first sight. The couple welcomed their first child together—daughter Summer Moon Honey—in April 2021 before tying the knot.

However, Shay revealed in her 2025 memoir My Good Side that the Australian athlete cheated on her in 2020 during her pregnancy, but only came clean about the affair during 2023's Scandoval controversy.

Longtime lovers Katie Maloney and Tom Schwartz got married in August 2016 after six years of dating. Their romance hit a speed bump in December 2024 when Kennedy was arrested for domestic vioence after an incident with Leviss. By the next month, the former couple announced they had broken up amid Kennedy's legal troubles, which did not result in any formal charges against him.

During the 10th season of VPR, Kent revealed she hadn't had sex since their breakup, but dove back into the dating pool by hooking up with a guy during a girls trip to Lake Havasu.

After a six-year romance with Sandoval—and her fling with Taylor—Doute dated Brian Carter on and off before moving on with Alex Menache. The pair ended their two-year romance in June 2022.

"We love each other," he shared in March 2024 of the vingtage clothing busniess owner, calling her "one of the coolest human beings on earth. The baddest b---h alive. She's got this unconventional sense of humor. She's sharp as hell, super successful."

However, their romance fizzled out by the following year, with Schwartz sharing on an April 2025 episode of his Detox Retox podcast, "We're really good friends."

"He just makes me feel really special, and he's really special," she shared of her new man on her Disrespectfully podcast in October 2024. "I'm just really, really happy."

"We work very well, we have similar goals and it feels like we could really grow together," he noted to Us Weekly the following year. "I feel so fortunate and lucky to have her in my life. She’s been my rock and stuck by me."

#846. European football: Barcelona roar back from two goals down to sink Villarreal

Barça prevail 3-2 despite Lamine Yamal’s missed penalty

Atalanta snatch point in thrilling 4-4 draw with Inter

Barcelona came back from two goals behind to beat Villarreal 3-2 at home on Sunday and restore their three-point lead at the top of La Liga.

Two goals inside seven minutes from Tajon Buchanan and Tani Oluwaseyi gave Villarreal a commanding lead at Camp Nou and things got worse for Barça when winger Lamine Yamal missed a first-half penalty.

The Catalan giants fought back in style, striking three times in an 11-minute second-half spell to claim victory. Gerard Martín and Fermín López pulled Barça level before Pau Navarro’s own goal gave them victory.

Barça have now won four consecutive matches across all competitions since their Clàsico defeat by Real Madrid in October, and restored their three-point cushion over José Mourinho’s side, who had moved level with Saturday’s victory over Celta Vigo.

Buchanan fired Villarreal ahead in the fifth minute, producing a perfect sliced effort from distance after López gave the ball away. Two minutes later, the visitors doubled their lead through another Canadian, as Oluwaseyi broke down the left flank and smashed an effort into the roof of the net.

Hansi Flick’s side should have pulled one back when Oluwaseyi felled Lamine Yamal in the area and a penalty was given after a VAR review. The teenager took it himself but dragged his spot-kick against the post and wide.

Barcelona came out invigorated for the second half and Peter Gulacsi saved López’s low effort before Martín headed home in the 57th minute from Pedri’s cross.

Four minutes later, López slammed home the second after being teed up by Lamine Yamal and the third was quick to follow. Lamine Yamal’s clever backheel pass fed Eric García, whose cross was bundled into the back of his own net by Navarro, who was later sent off for a second yellow card to complete a miserable afternoon.

Atlético Madrid stayed on the tail of Spain’s top two with a comfortable 3-0 derby win over Getafe.

Diego Simeone’s side are five points behind leaders Barcelona and two off Real Madrid. Álex Baena and Johnny Cardoso’s first-half goals, both set up by Julián Alvarez, got the job done away at the Coliseum stadium in the suburbs south of the Spanish capital.

Álex Grimaldo wrapped up the victory in stoppage time with a penalty, after Getafe’s Djene Dakonam was sent off for fouling Alexander Sørloth.

In Serie A, Atalanta rescued an extraordinary late 4-4 draw against Inter on Sunday as the champions fell three points off the title pace despite Pio Esposito’s hat-trick.

Inter looked comfortable in Bergamo when Petar Sucic’s penalty gave them a two-goal cushion in the 76th minute after Esposito’s goals, but Charles De Ketelaere’s second of the night and a stoppage-time Franck Kessié penalty salvaged a point.

It marked only the third time Inter have dropped points in the league this season, but kept Cristian Chivu’s side in third place, one point behind Roma and three adrift of leaders Lazio.

Esposito struck twice in the first half, pouncing on a deflected ball in the box to sweep home the opener before doubling Inter’s lead by heading home from a corner. Eljif Elmas quickly got one back for the hosts to keep the game alive, but Esposito took his third in composed fashion early in the second half, marking his eighth goal in five games for club and country.

De Ketelaere proved the catalyst for Atalanta’s fightback, pulling a goal back with a header and firing home a powerful finish either side of Sucic’s spot-kick.

That set up a thrilling conclusion as Atalanta chased what had seemed an unlikely point, which they claimed when a penalty was awarded for handball that Kessié calmly converted.

Juventus moved into the top six with a thumping 4-0 victory over Venezia as their recent upturn in form continued. Luciano Spalletti’s side were booed off after a goalless first half, but found four second-half strikes as their unbeaten run stretched to four games in all competitions.

Nick Woltemade sparked the game into life after coming off the bench, pouncing on a loose ball to smash home his second league goal in two games before turning provider for Teun Koopmeiners’ whipped finish. Juan Cabal headed home Juve’s third before Kolo Muani won and converted a penalty to complete the rout, with all four goals coming between the 53rd and 71st minute.

“In the first half, we gave the ball away too much,” Spalletti told Dazn. “It was crucial the players recognised something was missing … in the second half, the players were decisive and more relaxed.”

Milan returned to the top four as Gonçalo Ramos ended his goal drought in a 5-1 thrashing of Frosinone.

Ruben Amorim’s side sealed back-to-back wins for the first time in over a month to go fourth, five points behind leaders Lazio, as club record signing Ramos broke a five-match goalless streak.

Milan got off to a flying start with a Gabriele Calvani own goal and a composed Ramos strike inside 19 minutes. Amorim accused his players of “not helping Ramos” before the game after the Portugal international scored just twice in his first 11 league games following his summer move from Paris Saint-Germain.

His third was met with a loud roar from the San Siro crowd after he was teed up by Adrien Rabiot, who became the first Milan midfielder since Kaká in 2004 to notch a goal or assist in seven consecutive league games.

The visitors soon hit back through Patrizio Masini, but Milan pulled clear in the second half with some lethal counterattacking as substitutes Ardon Jashari and Alphadjo Cisse struck before Christian Pulisic’s dinked finish completed the biggest victory of the Amorim era.

Milutin Osmajic scored twice in a 2-0 win for Genoa at Sassuolo, while Bologna were held to a 1-1 draw by Udinese, who climb off the bottom of the table at Venezia’s expense.

In Ligue 1, Paris FC climbed to second place behind local rivals Paris Saint-Germain with a 4-0 home win over lowly Angers. Patrick Zabi, Luca Koleosho, Maxime Lopez and Diego Coppola all struck in the second half for Liam Rosenior’s high-flying side.

Le Mans struck five minutes into stoppage time to complete a stunning 3-2 comeback ⁠victory at Marseille to move ⁠clear of the ⁠relegation places.

Substitute ​Jean Vercruysse delivered the decisive blow to end Marseille’s run of five successive league victories.

Marseille appeared in complete control ⁠after Amine Gouiri scored for a fourth consecutive game and the Brazilian winger Igor Paixão doubled their lead during a dominant first half.

Louis Mafouta pulled one back with a powerful free-kick 20 ‌minutes from time, although he then had a penalty saved in the 78th minute. Erwan Colas equalised six minutes later before Vercruysse struck late to seal all three points.

Bayern Munich’s Jamal Musiala reportedly suffered another seizure in training this week, according to information received by an AFP subsidiary on Sunday.

Musiala collapsed twice on the pitch in pre-season with the 23-year-old later revealing he had a “neurological disorder” which can lead to “temporary but treatable seizures”. Last Monday’s incident was the second since he made the announcement; the player is reportedly adjusting his medication to properly treat the condition while continuing to play.

News of the incident comes as Bayern have faced criticism from footballers’ union Fifpro over what they claim is a “coordinated campaign” to pressure Musiala to renegotiate the contract he extended in 2025.

On Friday, Bayern’s supervisory board member and former chief executive Karl-Heinz Rummenigge suggested the Germany international may need to take a pay cut if he cannot recapture his old form.

“Based on what we know, it unfortunately suggests that it will be difficult for him to return to the level he so often demonstrated,” Rummenigge said. “If he doesn’t return to being the Jamal of old, then we need to have a conversation … because frankly, the current financial figures would no longer be justifiable.”

#844. Manchester City’s WSL title bid hit by Spurs after Vinberg and Naz’s late double

This most unpredictable and evenly contested Women’s Super League campaign took another unexpected twist as Manchester City missed the chance to return to the top of the table as they suffered a second successive defeat, by virtue of a terrific performance from a Tottenham side who moved within three points of the European places.

The shock result came just 24 hours after City’s title rivals Chelsea had dropped points at Liverpool. It was the first time City had failed to win a home league match during Andrée Jeglertz’s 16 months in charge, let alone lose.

Nevertheless, the victory was fully deserved for Tottenham, who made Khadija “Bunny” Shaw wait to equal her teammate Vivianne Miedema’s all-time WSL goalscoring record of 97 goals.

Jeglertz described the defeat as a “wake-up call” for his team, adding: “Tottenham were a little bit more urgent than us. Each duel counts, each moment counts, each ball counts. That was something that I missed with our players, especially in the second half where we needed to score and we needed to beat them in one-versus-one situations. I missed a little bit of that urgency, which I think is the most important in a team, and if we drop a little bit in that, this league is so tight and tough and the teams are so good, you will drop points and lose games.”

Before the game, the anticipated storyline felt almost too obvious. Shaw, needing three goals to surpass Miedema, was facing a club against whom she had scored four hat-tricks, including on Tottenham’s most recent visit to this stadium in March, when she recorded the WSL’s fastest treble. Persistently their tormentor, Shaw has scored more goals against Spurs than any other player has managed against a single opponent in the competition.

When Shaw opened the scoring inside 10 minutes, everything seemed to be following the script. Jade Rose, pressing very high up the pitch for a centre-back, won the ball and played a precise low pass across to Shaw, who tucked into the bottom corner from inside the box to record her 96th WSL goal and her 16th against Tottenham.

That, however, proved to be the only effort at goal – on or off target – that City would register during the opening 45 minutes, as Tottenham impressed. Kirsty Hanson drew a good save from Ayaka Yamashita and Hanson also felt she had a very strong claim for a penalty when Carlotta Wamser appeared to foul her inside the area, but it was not long before the visitors were deservedly level as Cathinka Tandberg expertly turned home Hanson’s cross with a clinical near-post finish.

Tottenham continued to threaten after the break, although Rose scooped over the bar to spurn a huge City chance on the rebound after a Lauren Hemp free-kick had been parried by Lize Kop. Some very effective counterattacking football then deservedly won the game for Tottenham as they scored twice to stun the defending champions.

First, in the 74th minute, an exquisite Drew Spence through ball found the run of Matilda Vinberg – who was a late addition to the starting side after the withdrawal of Olivia Holdt during the warm-up because of stomach pains – and Vinberg showed her quality to turn Rose and fire past Yamashita. Vinberg turned provider five minutes later, to set up Jessica Naz for another good finish.

No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football

Martin Ho, the Tottenham head coach, hailed his team’s “outstanding” display, saying: “Every time we play a team who has been in the top three consistently, the conversation is: ‘Can you get one over the line?’ And, for the players, they need to feel what that feels like and enjoy that. Today we nullified a lot of their threats. That will give us a lot of confidence.”

Manchester City had won 12 of their 13 previous WSL games against Tottenham, and all of their past 17 WSL home games, but this defeat added a further dent to their title challenge after their loss at Stamford Bridge last weekend. Chelsea, held to a goalless draw by Liverpool on Saturday, remain two points clear.

Arsenal remain winless at home in the WSL this season after being held to another frustrating draw at the Emirates, this time by West Ham. Arsenal had 22 shots at goal but were unable to break the deadlock, as their under-pressure head coach, Renée Slegers, oversaw a sixth home league draw out of six, leaving Arsenal eight points behind the top three.

Manchester United left it late to come from behind and beat Birmingham 2-1 but Simi Awujo’s last-gasp header from a corner gave them a valuable win and extended Eva Olid’s side’s club-record unbeaten run to 14 matches in all competitions. Birmingham had led inside four minutes through Lee Geum-min’s expert volley but Elisabeth Terland’s close-range finish with 10 minutes to go and Awujo’s 94th-minute winner snatched it, moving Olid’s fourth-placed team just six points off the top.

Elsewhere, the bottom side Charlton collected their first point of the season as they drew 1-1 with Aston Villa, while Brighton moved into the top half with a 1-0 victory at Everton, courtesy of Maz Pacheco’s early own goal. Tom Garry

Jeglertz continued: “We will bounce back, I’m not worried about that. I know the qualities in this group. But it’s the good habits, the small details that matter. Those are the things that win titles – this was actually the first time that I missed that in a game and I’m pretty sure it’s not going to happen again.” With just seven points now separating the top five, his team can ill-afford for it to happen again.

#842. Megaspeed and the battle to go high-end Nvidia chips into China

Jensen Huang's affair with a suspected Chinese spy has shone a light on Megaspeed, the company she worked for. It is under investigation in the US for smuggling Nvidia chips into China, which it denies.

As Nvidia, one of the world's most valuable companies, grapples with CEO Jensen Huang's romantic relationship with an alleged Chinese spy, attention is turning to the much smaller company she worked for.

Alice H., the alleged spy, worked as an executive for Megaspeed, a Singapore-based data center and AI computing company. It manages data center access, including for some major Chinese tech firms such as Alibaba.

According to Megaspeed's website as of November 2026, the company advertises itself as an "Nvidia cloud partner", saying it provides "computing power product services covering Nvidia's entire GPU product line." GPU stands for Graphic Processing Unit, a specialized electronic circuit that are in high demand for artificial intelligence (AI) applications, because they are designed to handle high numbers of parallel mathematical calculations. Megaspeed says it provides access for clients to Nvidia's advanced GB200 NVL72 ​computing system.

This type of firm is often referred to as a "neocloud". It buys Nvidia chips and computing power and then rents it out — in this case, at multiple sites across south-east Asia, to different companies. The US has set up strict export controls to prevent that Nvidia's high-performance chips end up in China, because it sees China as a competitor in the global AI race. It also does not want data centers made up of Nvidia chips to be owned by Chinese companies. It does, however, tolerate that data center compute with Nvidia chips be rented out to Chinese companies like Alibaba, and occasionally allows the export of Nvidia chips for specific purposes.

Megaspeed has bought billions of dollars worth of Nvidia's products in recent years and has been accused of breaching US export controls to divert Nvidia chips into China.

In December 2025, Bloomberg reported that the "once-obscure" Megaspeed had become the biggest buyer of Nvidia's chips in all of south-east Asia and that the US government was investigating its ownership structure and whether or not it was smuggling Nvidia chips into China.

At the same time, Singapore police began an investigation into whether or not Megaspeed had "violated local laws" without specifying which ones. Those investigations are believed to be still ongoing.

On December 23, 2025, Megaspeed strenuously denied any wrongdoing in a statement — which still appears as the first page for visitors to the company's website as of November 2026.

"There has been no evidence of any violations concerning the illicit transfer of chips or any illegal activities, and this demonstrates that we are a compliant and legitimate company," it said. "We operate fully within the bounds of all applicable export control regulations and maintain the highest standards of legal and ethical conduct."

The US government investigation began in 2024. The Commerce Department initially began looking into Megaspeed, but the US Justice Department has since taken over. According to the New York Times, this switch came about after an Nvidia executive directly contacted the Commerce Department about the investigation.

Megaspeed was founded in 2015 and was originally called 7Road International. It changed its name to Megaspeed in March 2023. It is owned by the Singapore-registered Swiftdata, which was set up in October 2023.

Its rise in prominence coincided with a sharp increase in assets, which increased from $33 million in 2023 to $3 billion in 2024.

Alice H., the woman accused of being a Chinese spy, had an affair with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. She is widely seen as an influential figurehead at Megaspeed. She also served as the company's managing director of Megaspeed for eight months in 2023.

The Financial Times reported on Monday that Alice H. leveraged her close access to Jensen Huang and Nvidia to pitch AI chips deals to Chinese investors.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

The newspaper said that in early 2025, Alice H. sought investment in China for a data center project in south-east Asia, and cited their easy access to Nvidia chips and close relationship with Alibaba.

Alibaba lent money to Megaspeed in June 2024, via subsidiaries. It has remained Megaspeed's largest client, according to reporting by the Financial Times.

In December 2025, Nvidia said its own inquiry into Megaspeed had found no evidence of chips being diverted and that the company was fully owned and operated outside of China, with no Chinese shareholders. The company told Bloomberg at the time that it had visited Megaspeed's facilities on multiple occasions and had seen nothing untoward.

Megaspeed is one of several companies accused of smuggling Nvidia's chips into China or finding ways to give Chinese companies access to them.

Nvidia's high-performance chips are seen as essential for companies looking for the most advanced form of supercomputing to use and develop various AI applications.

Back in 2022, the Biden Administration began severely restricting the sale of the US's most advanced chips to China, part of the two countries' growing rivalry to achieve AI dominance.

However, an illegal smuggling and underground network was soon set up, with many vendors operating to get the chips into China and selling them on to companies there.

In December 2025, US authorities shut down the operations of Hao Global, a US-based shell company with links to China which plead guilty to smuggling Nvidia chips to China.

In June 2026, Taiwanese government agencies raided the offices of Super Micro Computer as part of an investigation into the smuggling of Nvidia chips to China.

While export restrictions have been eased significantly under the Trump administration, there are still significant blocks and restrictions on the most advanced Nvidia chips.

In December 2025, the Trump administration approved several Chinese companies to buy or handle advanced Nvidia H200 chips, a move that sparked significant concern among the US security establishment.

However, that deal has not led to a significant flow of Nvidia chips moving legally to China, amid strict US licencing controls and official reluctance from Beijing to publicly promote Nvidia chips to the detriment of its own alternatives.

#841. Brooks Nader Reveals If She Approves of Sister Dating Pete Davidson

Brooks Nader addressed speculation that her sister Sarah Jane Nader is dating Pete Davidson during an exclusive interview with E! News at People and InStyle’s Drive-By Party in Las Vegas Nov. 20.

Brooks Nader loves thy sister Sarah Jane Nader, but she isn’t too thrilled about a potential update on her love life.

Amid rumors her younger sister is dating Pete Davidson, the Baywatch actress shared her thoughts on the speculation.

“I don’t approve of it. No,” Brooks exclusively told E! News at People and InStyle’s Drive-By Party at the Las Vegas Grand Prix Nov. 20 as she gave a thumbs-down to the camera. “She can do whatever she wants, but I’m not into it.”

And according to the 29-year-old, she’s not always privy to details about Sarah Jane’s dating life.

“You’d have to ask her,” Brooks said of how long her sister and Pete have been seeing each other. “She doesn’t get into it with me. When she knows I don’t approve of someone, she doesn’t tell me anything, so I find out online.”

While the Sports Illustrated model made her views on Sarah Jane potentially dating the comedian clear, a source close to Pete previously told E! News there is no truth to the dating rumors.

In fact, while it’s been nearly four months since the Dancing With the Stars alum and Bodies Bodies Bodies actor made waves when they stepped out together in Brooklyn, the source noted that they’ve only seen each other a handful of times since.

For the August outing, Sarah Jane, 24, and Pete, 33, were spotted getting into a car together. The Meet Cute actor opened the passenger door for the Love They Nader star, before he moved over to the driver’s side. But at the time, a source with direct knowledge told E! News the duo are just friends.

As for Brooks, the news of her sister hanging out with Pete—dad to daughter Scottie, 11 months, with ex Elsie Hewitt—was unexpected.

“Oh wow, I thought she was into girls this week,” she joked to TMZ after Sarah Jane and Pete’s night out. “That’s what her vibe has been.”

The model added that she needed to chat with Sarah Jane, jokingly admitting that she was “confused” and “lost” about the rumors.

“I really did think that she was into girls recently,” Brooks quipped, “but she keeps us on our toes.”

While it’s unclear what the future will hold for Sarah Jane’s love life, keep reading for a closer look at Brooks’ dating history…

Leaving her Louisiana home to pursue her modeling dreams at the age of 19, Brooks Nader knew she had to make some big deals. "When I moved to New York, my dad was like, 'You're living a full-ride scholarship. I have no money to support your life in New York. You better find a boyfriend,'" she explained to People. "Which I did, thank God, for just the rent purposes."

Though, she arguably grew quite fond of advertising executive Billy Haire, the duo marrying in New Orleans' French Quarter in December 2019.

Her mom and dad were less than thrilled to hear about their separation nearly five years later. "When I told my parents I was getting divorced, you’d think I killed somebody," she shared on the Love Thy Nader reality series she filmed with sisters Sarah Jane Nader, Grace Ann Nader and Mary Holland Nader. "They were like, 'This is the worst decision ever. Divorce is a sin.'"

But the Sports Illustrated Swimsuit model would beg to differ. "Once I got to that other side, I realized, 'Wait, I got me. I can do anything I f--king put my mind to,'" she reflected to Bustle in 2025. "I was with someone for 10 years, and I cut it off and came out better. I can push out a human; I can start a company; I can get over anybody. It’s euphoric, that feeling."

As for Billy, he went on to charm another reality star, he and Southern Charm alum Naomie Olindo announcing their engagement in December 2025.

In the months following Brooks' divorce, it seemed she had snagged a pass from retired NFL quarterback Tom Brady. Though she and the NFL on Fox color commentator were spotted at Michael Rubin’s 2024 Fourth of July party in the Hamptons, any fireworks had dissipated by fall.

"She’s having fun as a single girl," sister Sarah Jane told Daily Mail that September. "I think it’s as exciting as it possibly could be."

Cast on Dancing With the Stars shortly after her 2024 divorce, Brooks was eyeing more than just the mirrorball trophy. Paired with pro Gleb Savchenko, the two quickly became partners IRL as well.

But much like their dances, their romance was largely physical. Single for the first time since she was 18, and doing the tango with "the hottest guy I've ever seen in my life," she detailed on Love Thy Nader, meant things escalated quickly.

"All we did was have sex," Brooks shared on the Freeform series, "because I didn't really talk to him that much."

Perhaps that lack of communication is why he felt blindsided when she confirmed in April 2025 that they were no longer in step.

They weren't even following the same routine, to be honest. "I was surprised to learn through an article published today … that Brooks has ended our relationship," Gleb said in an April 7 statement to Us Weekly. "The last communication I received from her was a text on April 6, asking to speak. I called her today in response, but she has not replied."

Jimmy Kimmel took a swing at getting Nader to confirm the rumors she was matched up with tennis phenom Jannik Sinner. "Are you dating Italian superstar Jannik Sinner?" he asked during her September 2025 appearance on Jimmy Kimmel Live. Her response? "Is this like an interrogation? I'm so scared right now."

Though she suggested Stephen Colbert could potentially serve up the truth. "Well, ask Stephen what match we were at," she said of sitting next to the late-night host during her Aug. 31 outing to the U.S. Open. Because, as she noted of Sinner, "I don't think he was at that one. You're close. You're warm, but we weren't at that match."

What Brooks was trying to hint at in her back-and-forth volley on Kimmel was that she'd found a potential partner in Spanish athlete Carlos Alcaraz. "The rumors are true," sister Grace Ann exclusively told E! News at the Raising Cane's New York Fashion Week Show days later. Still, she cautioned it wasn't exactly love-all just yet. "Dating is such a loose term," she added. "But I do know he’s the man of the hour."

And while she was waiting for an introduction, he'd already made the acquaintance of their other sisters. "I'm dying to," Grace Ann said of meeting the seven-time Grand Slam champ. "Such a cutie."

As for those finding fault with the swimsuit model doubling up with the tennis stars, "I mean, dating is such a loose term these days," she mused during a September 2025 appearance on Watch What Happens Live. "Guys do it all the time. So why can’t I do it?"

Oh, how it felt so real when Rocketman actor Taron Egerton held his tiny dancer close during a March 28, 2026 date night in Los Angeles. Following a three-hour dinner at Capo in Santa Monica, Calif., he and Brooks walked arm-in-arm to nearby Shutters on the Beach to drink each other in.
