#759. Morgan Wallen, Garth Brooks, Taylor Swift & More Artists With Most Weeks at No. 1 on Top Country Albums Chart: Full List

Male solo artists dominate, though three female solo artists and two groups have also achieved the feat.

Morgan Wallen’s I’m the Problem leads Billboard‘s Top Country Albums chart (dated Nov. 28) for the 54th nonconsecutive week. This ups Wallen’s career tally of weeks at No. 1 to 240, allowing him to extend his lead as the artist with the most weeks at No. 1 in the chart’s 62-year history.

Wallen’s achievement is especially impressive because he has amassed this hefty total of weeks at No. 1 in such a short amount of time. He first topped the chart a little more than six years ago — on Aug. 15, 2020.

I’m the Problem is Wallen’s third album to log a full year at No. 1 on Top Country Albums. Dangerous: The Double Album clung to the top spot for 97 weeks from 2021-23. One Thing at a Time led for 87 weeks from 2023-25. No other artist has spent 52 weeks on top with one album, much less three.

Top Country Albums originated as Hot Country Albums in the Jan. 11, 1964 issue of Billboard. Johnny Cash’s Ring of Fire (The Best of Johnny Cash) headed the inaugural chart. The compilation was well-timed: “Ring of Fire” had headed Hot Country Songs for seven weeks the previous summer and had crossed over to reach the top 20 on the Billboard Hot 100.

The chart was named Hot Country LP’s from 1968 to 1984, when vinyl LPs were king.

Twenty-one artists have logged 50 or more weeks at No. 1 on Top Country Albums. Male solo artists dominate, as you might expect, though three female solo artists have achieved the feat, as have two groups. (One of those groups is an all-female group.) Only one Black artist has amassed 50 or more weeks at No. 1, though that may change as country becomes more inclusive.

Here’s a look at all artists who have topped Top Country Albums for 50 or more weeks.

Longest-running No. 1: When the Sun Goes Down (14 weeks in 2004)

Notes: Chesney’s tally of No. 1 albums includes two live albums, LIVE: Live Those Songs Again (2006) and Live in No Shoes Nation (2017).

Longest-running No. 1: Blue (28 weeks in 1996-97)

Notes: Rimes’ total includes a 1997 compilation of early recordings, Unchained Melody: The Early Years. Rimes was just 14 in February 1997 when she won a Grammy for best new artist. She remains the youngest winner ever in that category.

Longest-running No. 1: My World (17 weeks in 1965-66)

Notes: My World was the first country album to receive a Grammy nod for album of the year. The album included the crossover hit “Make the World Go Away,” which all but defined the “countrypolitan” sound.

Longest-running No. 1: Wichita Lineman (20 weeks in 1968-69)

Notes: Wichita Lineman is tied with Johnny Cash at San Quentin for the longest run at No. 1 of any album in the 1960s. Campbell’s tally of No. 1 albums also includes Bobbie Gentry & Glen Campbell, a collab with the singer of “Ode to Billie Joe.” The 1968 album was the first collaborative album to reach No. 1 on the chart.

Longest-running No. 1: Pancho & Lefty (with Willie Nelson) (eight weeks in 1983)

Notes: Haggard’s tally of No. 1s includes eight albums on which his backing group, The Strangers, was also credited. Hag’s tally includes three live albums, Okie From Muskogee (1970), The Fightin’ Side of Me (1970)and I Love Dixie Blues … So I Recorded ‘Live’ in New Orleans (1973). It also includes two collabs with Willie Nelson, Pancho & Lefty and Django and Jimmie (2015).

Most recent week at No. 1: April 12, 2014

Longest-running No. 1: Johnny Cash at San Quentin (20 weeks in 1969)

Notes: Cash’s No. 1 albums spanned more than 50 years. Johnny Cash at San Quentin (which received a Grammy nod for album of the year) has had the longest run at No. 1 of any live album. It is also tied with Glen Campbell’s Wichita Lineman as the longest-running No. 1 album of the 1960s. Cash also reached No. 1 with two other live albums – Johnny Cash at Folsom Prison (1968) and The Johnny Cash Show (1970), which was recorded at the Grand Ole Opry. He also topped the chart with a 1985 collab LP with Willie Nelson, Waylon Jennings and Kris Kristofferson and with two posthumous albums – American V: A Hundred Highways (2006) and Out Among the Stars (2014).

Most recent week at No. 1: April 20, 1968

Longest-running No. 1: I’ve Got a Tiger by the Tail (15 weeks in 1965)

Notes: Owens’ first No. 1 album, Buck Owens Sings Tommy Collins (1964), was a tribute album to the singer/songwriter whose biggest hits included “You Better Not Do That” and “If You Can’t Bite, Don’t Growl.” Owens’ tally of No. 1 albums includes two live albums, Carnegie Hall Concert (1966) and Buck Owens and His Buckaroos in Japan! (1967).

Most recent week at No. 1: April 13, 2019

Longest-running No. 1s: Ocean Front Property (six weeks in 1987) and Carrying Your Love With Me (six weeks in 1997)

Notes: Strait made this list the hard way – without a single album that logged more than six weeks at No. 1. Strait’s tally of No. 1 albums includes the 1992 soundtrack to Pure Country, in which he starred.

Longest-running No. 1: Fly (36 weeks in 1999-2000)

Notes: The Chicks, formerly Dixie Chicks, are the second-highest ranking group on this list. Three of the group’s No. 1 albums – Fly, Home and Taking the Long Way – received Grammy nods for album of the year. The latter album won the award. The group’s most recent No. 1 album, Gaslighter, was bumped from the top spot by the debut album by a promising newcomer named Morgan Wallen.

Longest-running No. 1: Greatest Hits (16 weeks in 1979)

Notes: Jennings’ tally of No. 1 albums includes three collabs with Nelson – one just with Nelson; one that also included Jessi Colter and Tompall Glaser; and one that included Johnny Cash and Kris Kristofferson as well. His tally also includes a 1976 live album, Waylon Live.

Longest-running No. 1: Not a Moment Too Soon (29 weeks in 1994)

Notes: McGraw’s tally includes a 2017 collab with his wife, Faith Hill, The Rest of Our Life. That title should probably be The Rest of Our Lives, but we’re not going to correct the grammar of someone who has logged 76 weeks at No. 1.

Longest-running No. 1: Always & Forever (43 weeks in 1987-88)

Notes: Always & Forever had the longest run at No. 1 of any album in the 1980s.

Longest-running No. 1s: Charley Pride Sings Heart Songs (16 weeks in 1972) and The Best of Charley Pride, Volume 2 (16 weeks in 1972).

Notes:  The albums referenced above were No. 1 back-to-back and spent a combined total of 32 consecutive weeks at No. 1. Now, that’s what you call dominating a chart. Both albums contained Pride’s signature song, “Kiss an Angel Good Mornin.’” Pride’s final No. 1 album, There’s a Little Bit of Hank in Me (1980), was a tribute to Hank Williams. Pride is the only Black artist on this list so far.

Longest-running No. 1: This One’s for You (50 weeks in 2017-18)

Notes: This One’s for You had the longest run at No. 1 of any album in the 2010s.

Longest-running No. 1: Come on Over (50 weeks in 1997-2000)

Notes: Twain is the second-highest ranking female solo artist on this list. Come on Over had the longest run at No. 1 of any album in the 1990s. The hit-studded blockbuster spent time at No. 1 in four consecutive years – 1997 through 2000. It received a Grammy nod for album of the year, and spawned two song of the year nominees, “You’re Still the One” and “You’ve Got a Way.”

Longest-running No. 1: Kenny (25 weeks in 1979-80)

Notes: Kenny, which housed the hit “You Decorated My Life,” had the longest run at No. 1 of any album in the 1970s. Rogers’ tally includes a 1978 collab with Dottie West, Every Time Two Fools Collide, and a 2018 compilation, The Best of Kenny Rogers: Through the Years, which hit No. 1 following his death in March 2020.

Most recent week at No. 1: July 29, 2023?

Longest-running No. 1: Fearless (35 weeks in 2008-09)

Notes:  Swift is the highest-charting female solo artist on this list, which is especially impressive given her mid-career pivot to pop. Her tally includes both the original and Taylor’s Version’s editions of Fearless, Speak Now and Red. With Fearless, Swift became the youngest Grammy winner for album of the year to that point, a title now held by Billie Eilish.

Longest-running No. 1: Always on My Mind (22 weeks in 1982)

Notes: Nelson’s tally includes a collab with Waylon Jennings, Jessi Colter and Tompall Glaser; another with Jennings, Johnny Cash and Kris Kristofferson; another with just Jennings, and two with Haggard. It also includes two live albums, Willie and Family Live (1979) and the Honeysuckle Rose soundtrack (1980).

Longest-running No. 1s: Feels So Right (28 weeks in 1981-82) and Mountain Music (28 weeks in 1982-83).

Notes: Alabama is the highest-ranking group on this list. Feels So Right (in May 1981) was the first No. 1 by a group that wasn’t named after its leader. (So, we’re discounting Merle Haggard and the Strangers, Sonny James and the Southern Gentlemen and The Charlie Daniels Band.) Alabama’s tally of No. 1 albums includes a 1988 live album, Alabama Live.

Longest-running No. 1: No Fences (41 weeks in 1990-91)

Notes: Brooks’ tally of No. 1 albums includes a double-disc live album, Double Live (1998); a pair of Christmas albums, Garth Brooks & the Magic of Christmas (1999) and Christmas Together (2016), the latter a collab with his wife, Trisha Yearwood; and a remarkable four box sets – The Limited Series (1998), Blame It All on My Roots: Five Decades of Influences (2013), The Ultimate Collection (2016) and The Anthology Part I: The First Five Years (2017).

Longest-running No. 1: Dangerous: The Double Album (97 weeks in 2021-23)

Notes: Dangerous: The Double Album had the longest run at No. 1 in the chart’s history. One Thing at a Time, which spent 87 weeks at No. 1, is in second place. I’m the Problem is in third place.

#757. Leonid meteor shower thrills stargazers worldwide with colorful sky show (photos/video)

From colorful meteors to lingering trails, the Leonids put on a great show this year.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The Leonid meteor shower put on quite the show this week, with bright, colorful meteors thrilling stargazers worldwide and we've got the photos to prove it.

The annual meteor shower peaked overnight on Nov. 17-18, with photographers braving chilly temperatures, clouds and even fog in hopes of catching the perfect shot. And for some, their patience certainly paid off.

Leonids occur when Earth passes through debris left behind by comet 55P/Tempel-Tuttle, which orbits the sun approximately every 33 years. As tiny pieces of comet debris enter Earth's atmosphere at speeds of up to 44 miles (71 kilometers) per second, they burn up, producing bright streaks of light.

The meteor shower is also famous for producing some of the most spectacular meteor storms in history. In fact, this year marks the 60th anniversary of the great Leonid meteor storm of 1966, when observers reported an astonishing 40 meteors per second at the peak. To mark the occasion, we spoke to people who witnessed the extraordinary event first-hand and you can read their remarkable accounts in our special feature.

But back to the present! Let's take a look at some of the best photographs and videos captured during this year's impressive display.

Photographer Austin Rebello drove several hours to Nubble Lighthouse in York, Maine, to meet up with fellow astrophotographer Rob Wright and hopefully capture a Leonid or two.

"I specifically drove a few hours up there for hopes of capturing exactly this, as the radiant of the Leonids rose behind the lighthouse," Rebello told Space.com in an email.

"My friend and I were lucky enough to also see it with our eyes, and it was definitely a top 3 meteor for me, as it was even bright enough to briefly cast shadows."

Rebello also revealed on X that the meteor left behind a vibrant blue trail that remained visible to the naked eye for more than 30 seconds.

Fellow astrophotographer Rob Wright was also at Nubble Lighthouse that night, where he captured the lingering trail of a particularly bright meteor on camera for an incredible 12 minutes, according to a post on X.

"Turns out the smoke from the bright meteor early this morning was visible on camera for TWELVE (12) MINUTES just lingering there," Wright wrote on X.

Turns out the smoke from the bright meteor early this morning was visible on camera for TWELVE (12) MINUTES just lingering there. I was able to make a rough timelapse video to show this. -- November 18, 2026 York, Maine https://t.co/pm9htHcMm3November 18, 2026

This phenomenon is known as a persistent meteor train and is created when a bright meteor leaves behind a trail of ionized gas that continues to glow long after the meteor itself has disappeared. These ghostly trails usually fade relatively quickly, but some, like this one, can persist for several minutes. They can twist and change shape as they're carried along by winds high in Earth's atmosphere, according to the BBC Sky at Night Magazine.

Meanwhile, over Deming, New Mexico, photographer Greg Gage had to contend with rather less favorable conditions as clouds and unexpected fog rolled in during the meteor shower's peak.

"While it was perfectly clear when I set up the camera, the night turned out to be mostly cloudy with some light fog," Gage told Space.com in an email.

"But it was just a thin veil and made for some interesting effects. I did catch one meteor through the fog."

But the fog wasn't the only surprise Gage encountered. He also managed to capture a particularly colorful meteor as it blazed through the sky.

"One meteor was rather dramatic. It went through multiple colors as it traveled through the atmosphere," Gage continued.

Gage captured the photographs with a Nikon D5500 and a 14mm lens.

And the colorful displays weren't limited to North America.

In Japan, astronomer Daichi Fujii, curator of the Hiratsuka City Museum, captured a spectacular Leonid fireball streaking across the sky above Hiratsuka in the early hours of Nov. 19.

The brilliant fireball left behind a glowing trail that changed from green to orange as it lingered in the sky.

さきほど、しし座流星群の大火球が流れました。2026年11月19日4時35分2秒に、平塚から北の低い空に向けたカメラでとらえた様子です。緑色のアフターグローからオレンジ色の永続痕まで、美しく色を変化させました。 https://t.co/Q5ihqCPtX2November 18, 2026

A fireball is defined as an unusually bright meteor that reaches a visual magnitude of -3 or brighter, according to NASA's Center for Near Earth Object Studies.

Elsewhere in Japan, skywatcher @simao had a particularly productive night, capturing an impressive 92 meteors between 10:17 p.m. local time on Nov. 18 and 5:40 a.m. on Nov. 19, from central Saitama Prefecture.

昨夜から今朝にかけて捉えた流星は正味92個でした。 11/18 22:17 〜 11/19 05:40 埼玉県中央から #atomcam #meteordetect #火球 #流星 https://t.co/jRzsHdQ7MVNovember 19, 2026

But that wasn't all simao captured that night! At 2:19 a.m. on Nov. 19, they caught both a Leonid meteor and a sprite at the same time, looking northwest.

Sprites are very difficult to capture, as they appear as fleeting flashes of light high above thunderstorms, typically appearing as red, jellyfish-like structures.

昨夜の流星とスプライト、初めて同じタイミングで撮れた。 11/19 02:19:36 埼玉県中央から北西の空 #atomcam #meteordetect #火球 #流星 #スプライト https://t.co/LBipTuoM0LNovember 19, 2026

The Leonids were already making an appearance in the days leading up to the shower's peak.

On Nov. 16, astrophotographer @EricTheSpaceCat captured several possible Leonids streaking through the sky.

Meteors from last night/this morning. Cropped to show detail. A lot of possible Leonids. The Leonid meteor shower is active and peaks the night of 11/17-11/18. https://t.co/s7YsvKdvECNovember 15, 2026

A likely Leonid meteor from yesterday morning. The Leonid meteor shower peaks tonight! Good luck if you go out to watch. https://t.co/xxbEV32NQlNovember 17, 2026

If the Leonids have left you wanting more, you won't have to wait long for another significant meteor shower! Next up are the Geminids, one of the most prolific meteor showers of the year, which will peak overnight on Dec. 13-14. And 2026 is shaping up to be a particularly good year for them. With only a slender waxing crescent moon in the sky, moonlight interference will be minimal, giving skywatchers a chance to spot up to 120 Geminid meteors per hour under ideal conditions.

For the best views, head somewhere dark, away from city lights, and give your eyes around 30 minutes to adjust to the darkness.

Editor's Note: If you snap an impressive night sky photo and would like to share it with Space.com's readers, send your photo(s), comments, and your name and location to spacephotos@space.com.

Daisy Dobrijevic joined Space.com in February 2022, having previously worked as a staff writer for All About Space magazine. She completed an editorial internship with BBC Sky at Night Magazine and worked at the National Space Centre, communicating space science to the public.

Daisy holds a PhD in plant physiology and a Master's in Environmental Science. Based in Nottingham, U.K., she covers all things space, with a special focus on solar activity and space weather. She also has a keen interest in astrotourism and is always on the lookout for the next northern lights adventure.

She will join Hurtigruten as an onboard astronomer for a northern lights sailing in January 2027.

#756. Hungary eases abortion restrictions in women's rights overhaul

The reforms mark a break the the conservative policies of former PM Viktor Orban. The controversial "heartbeat regulation" is to be scrapped and women are to be better protected against violence.

Hungary on Thursday said it would ease abortion rules and ratify an international treaty on violence against women.

Under the planned changes to the so-called "heartbeat regulation," women will no longer be forced to listen to the vital signs of the fetus before an abortion.

Women will also be able to get emergency contraceptive pills without prescription.

The changes proposed by the new government under Prime Minister Peter Magyar are a significant break with the conservative policies of his predecessor Viktor Orban.

The country also plans to ratify the Istanbul Convention, a treaty aimed at preventing violence against women and domestic violence.

Hungarian law allows for most abortions to be performed up to 12 weeks, and up to 24 weeks in cases of severe developmental abnormalities. Until now, women were required to have a medical provider show them evidence of a definitive sign of fetal life, commonly understood as the so-called "fetal heartbeat," before deciding whether to have an abortion.

The controversial 2022 policy had received widespread criticism from doctors and women’s rights groups as being cruel and humiliating. It will now be scrapped.

The policy had not led to a decline in abortions and according to Magyar, had raised "serious bioethical questions."

The second major change is that emergency contraception will be available without prescription.

Further measures include changing the criminal code aimed at better protecting women, including making the misuse of intimate images a criminal offense and strengthening the treatment of victims of domestic violence during criminal proceedings.

Hungary also plans to ratify an international treaty on the protection of women which most other EU members have long ratified. The Istanbul Convention came into force in 2014 and, among other things, requires rape to be criminalized based on the absence of freely given consent.

"We are making it clear that sexual acts can only ⁠take ​place with the voluntary consent of the other party," ​Magyar said.

The government of his predecessor Orban had opposed the treaty, arguing that it promoted what it described as "gender ideology."

"We are making a clear and accountable commitment to putting an end to the era of inaction," Magyar said in a Facebook video.

Among the EU’s other members, only Bulgaria, the Czech Republic, Lithuania and Slovakia have not yet ratified the convention.

The Istanbul Convention is a treaty by the Council of Europe, an international organization that promotes human rights and the rule of law across Europe and includes more countries than the member of the EU.

#755. ‘Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping’ Slays $120M at Box Office as Franchise Heats Back Up

The sixth film in the Lionsgate series rebounded after 2023's 'The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes,' while freshly expanded 'I Play Rocky' and newcomer 'Elsinore' also came out swinging.

The Hunger Games franchise has been revived at the box office. Meanwhile, I Play Rocky demonstrated major strength as it expanded wide with a rare A+ CinemaScore, and Elsinore notched a promising per-screen average in limited release.

Lionsgate released The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping in 4,018 North American theaters, and the sixth film in the dystopian franchise grossed $120 million in its opening weekend. This gives it the fourth-best debut in franchise history, besting 2015’s second Mockingjay movie ($102.6 million) and 2023 prequel The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes ($44.6 million) but behind 2013’s Catching Fire ($158 million), 2012’s series-launching The Hunger Games ($152.5 million) and 2014’s first Mockingjay ($121.8 million). Its $56 million domestic sum on Friday gave Sunrise the third-best debut Friday in franchise history, behind Catching Fire and The Hunger Games.

The new film added $105 million from 84 international territories for a global haul of $225 million.

Its audience was 67 percent female, with 50 percent of the crowd above age 25, according to PostTrak. Sunrise earned an A- CinemaScore from audiences, putting it below the A grades of the Jennifer Lawrence-led initial 2012 movie that kicked off the series and 2013’s Catching Fire but matching the A- grades of the two Mockingjay films.

The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping will notch the fifth-biggest opening in Lionsgate history, as it also stands at No. 5 among 2026 domestic openings for all studios. It represents the highest-grossing launch for the careers of stars Glenn Close, Jesse Plemons, Kieran Culkin and Elle Fanning. This weekend’s haul also brings the Hunger Games franchise’s box office total to roughly $3.437 billion to make it the studio’s highest-grossing franchise ever, topping The Twilight Saga.

Lionsgate had projected The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping to gross north of $80 million, but other sources expected that it would collect between $100 million and $130 million. Adapting author Suzanne Collins’ prequel novel that was published last year, director Francis Lawrence‘s movie carries a production budget of roughly $150 million as it revitalizes the franchise by telling a story set 24 years before the events of Collins’ original 2008 book.

This opening represents a major comeback for the series after registering its lowest-performing entry with 2023 prequel The Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes, given that Sunrise on the Reaping opened with more than double its launch. Starring Tom Blyth, Rachel Zegler and Hunter Schafer, Songbirds & Snakes — telling the backstory for the villainous President Snow, played by Ralph Fiennes in the new movie — disappointed, opening to $44 million domestically for the weekend before ending its run with $166.4 million domestically and a global sum of $361.8 million. It earned a B+ CinemaScore, the lowest for the franchise.

“When you have filmmaking giants as talented as Francis Lawrence [and producers] Nina Jacobson and Brad Simpson guiding the vision established by the brilliant creator Suzanne Collins, who started it all, you are in enormously capable hands,” Lionsgate film chief Adam Fogelson said in a statement. “This success is a testament to their remarkable film, the performances of our incredibly talented cast, and ultimately, the love of Hunger Games fans worldwide, who embraced a film that told a story they had been asking to see for many years.”

Sunrise on the Reaping holds a 67 percent critical score on Rotten Tomatoes, lagging behind the franchise’s first four movies but besting the 64 percent approval for Songbirds & Snakes. The new film has a franchise-best 95 audience score on Rotten Tomatoes. In his review for The Hollywood Reporter, chief film critic David Rooney wrote that it “delivers on emotion and brutal spectacle.”

The movie opened the day after the launch of the hotly anticipated video game Grand Theft Auto 6, which did not appear to prevent the film from thriving. Joseph Zada stars as Haymitch Abernathy, providing the backstory for the character whom Woody Harrelson brought to life in the first four movies. The cast for Sunrise on the Reaping also includes Mckenna Grace, Whitney Peak and Maya Hawke.

Overall, the domestic box office grossed $168 million from all titles this weekend, representing a major 89.4 percent boost over the previous frame, which saw Johnny Depp’s Ebenezer lead the group that collected a combined $88.7 million, according to Rentrak. This weekend is down 8.2 percent from the equivalent 2025 frame, which saw the launch of Wicked: For Good. This year’s domestic box office has reached $8.97 billion, marking a 20 percent improvement over 2025.

Among other weekend titles, Amazon MGM Studios expanded I Play Rocky to 2,477 North American locations after two frames in limited release. Peter Farrelly’s Rocky origin story earned a healthy $9.3 million to bring its domestic total to $10.4 million. The crowd skewed male at 56 percent, as 33 percent of moviegoers were age 55 and above.

Starring Anthony Ippolito as a young Sylvester Stallone, I Play Rocky landed a rare A+ CinemaScore, becoming only the second release this year to do so (after April’s A Great Awakening). I Play Rocky holds an 89 percent approval rating from critics on Rotten Tomatoes and a 98 percent audience score. Rooney’s review described it as a “big-hearted movie about moviemaking, if not an artful one.”

In its sophomore frame, Paramount’s horror-tinged holiday offering Ebenezer claimed third place with roughly $7.7 million for a decline of around 59 percent, bringing its domestic cume to $32.5 million. Depp marks his studio comeback vehicle with director Ti West’s reimagining of Charles Dickens’ A Christmas Carol, which opened atop last weekend’s box office.

Continuing to draw families in its third weekend is Warner Bros.’ The Cat in the Hat, as the animated adaptation of Dr. Seuss’ classic children’s book grossed around $6.9 million for a domestic total of $47.1 million. This marks a respectable decline of roughly 39 percent for directors Erica Rivinoja and Alessandro Carloni’s movie that features the voice of Bill Hader in the lead role. It is set to face fresh competition in the animated space from Disney’s Hexed over the forthcoming Thanksgiving frame.

Gkids and Toho’s Godzilla Minus Zero is likely to close out the top five with $2.6 million in its third weekend to reach a domestic cume of around $54.5 million.

A24’s Elizabeth Holmes documentary You Can See Everything is expected to place sixth with $2.5 million in its sixth weekend for a domestic total of $93.4 million. Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim’s feature has begun rolling out internationally and has surpassed the $100 million mark at the global box office, with Sony Pictures handling distribution for some international territories.

Focus Features opened Elsinore in six theaters in New York and Los Angeles, with director Simon Stone’s Oscar hopeful collecting approximately $240,000. Its impressive average of $40,000 per screen puts it in the top five for 2026 releases. Andrew Scott stars in the biographical film about Scottish actor Ian Charleson, who navigates personal challenges while preparing for a pivotal performance of Hamlet. Hailing from StudioCanal, Elsinore earned acclaim at Telluride and TIFF and holds an 87 percent rating from critics on Rotten Tomatoes, with Rooney deeming it “a hymn to the theater, powered by a towering lead turn.”

Toward the bottom of the top 10 is Ramayana: Rise of a Legend, with Sony Pictures distributing the Prime Focus Studios religious epic that is expected to gross $2 million for its third weekend to bring its domestic take to $28.4 million through Sunday. Director Nitesh Tiwari’s project becomes the highest-grossing Indian film ever at the North American box office, while it stands at No. 5 on the all-time global chart for Indian releases with a worldwide cume of $183 million.

With Thanksgiving arriving next weekend, the holiday frame brings an array of new options, including Disney’s Hexed, Universal’s Meet the Parents sequel Focker-in-Law, Netflix’s The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth and Angel’s biographical Hershey.

This story was first published on Nov. 21 at 8:16 a.m.

#754. Fans Choose LISA’s ‘Leave With Me’ as This Week’s Favorite New Music

Her latest solo release brought in more than 84% of the vote.

“Leave With Me,” the emotional new solo single released by LISA of BLACKPINK, tops this week’s new music poll.

Listeners voted in a poll published Friday (Nov. 20) on Billboard, choosing LISA’s latest track as their favorite new music.

“Leave With Me” topped new releases from TOMORROW X TOGETHER, Gracie Abrams and more on the poll, and it rose above the Grand Theft Auto VI album, which features songs by a number of stars: Cardi B, Dua Lipa, Lana Del Rey, Playboi Carti, Travis Scott, Morgan Wallen, Tame Impala and many others — including BLACKPINK member JENNIE (with “Power Trip”). At the poll’s closing time on Sunday, LISA’s new ballad had a landslide victory, bringing in more than 84% of the vote.

“Leave With Me” plays over the end credits of LISA’s Always Lalisa documentary about the rise of her career of a solo artist outside of girl group BLACKPINK. The doc, directed by Sue Kim, is now available to stream exclusively on YouTube Premium.

The song, officially released this week, was co-written by LISA, Feli Ferraro, Tyler Spry, Ali Tamposi and Shintaro Yasuda.

“The only way forward is through,” she sings, leading up to the chorus: “I’ma take yesterday, kiss it goodbye/ Wipe my eyes dry, hold my head high/ I leave with me/ Check the clock, yeah, it’s my time/ Spread my wings, fly, me on my side/ You know that there’s no hard feelings/ Every wrong and right, put me right where I’m supposed to be/ No hard feelings/ And you can come or stay, either way, I’ma leave with me.”

Prior to its release, LISA had surprised fans with the live debut of the then-unknown “Leave With Me” during opening night of her six-show “Viva La Lisa” residency at The Colosseum at Caesars Palace in Las Vegas.

Trailing behind “Leave With Me” on the poll are TOMORROW X TOGETHER’s “Angel Bite,” with 8% of the vote, and the multi-artist Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album, with 2% of the vote.

#753. Tom Jackson, Denver Broncos’ All-Pro Linebacker and ESPN Analyst, Dies at 75

He spent nearly 30 years with the network, often teaming with Chris Berman: “We’ve lost one of the best human beings ever to walk the planet.”

Tom Jackson, who parlayed a 14-season stint as a stalwart linebacker on the Denver Broncos’ famed “Orange Crush” defense into a long career as a popular football analyst on ESPN, has died. He was 75.

Jackson died Friday, his family told the network. No cause was announced.

Jackson was best known for his work alongside Chris Berman on the ESPN shows NFL Primetime and Sunday NFL Countdown, where the pair would deliver their humorous, entertaining take on highlights from games. Related Stories Music Peak Halftime Show: The A-List Machine Eventizing Pro Games Movies Lance Broadway, Pitcher Turned 'Olympus Has Fallen' Actor, Dies at 43

“All of us are stunned,” Berman said in a statement. “I’m stunned, we’re stunned and you’re stunned. We’ve lost one of the best human beings ever to walk the planet, Tom Jackson. I was fortunate to work side by side with Tom for 30 years … It was a labor of love for our whole team, both in front of the camera and behind it. We always hoped our viewers enjoyed the shows as much as we did bringing it to them every week.”

Berman said on Sunday NFL Countdown that Jackson’s death was unexpected and that he had spoken with his best friend “at length” on Tuesday. “He was a vital 75,” he said. On Nov. 1, they spent time on the ESPN set after Jackson arrived for a surprise visit.

“Tom was so much more than an accomplished NFL analyst,” Berman said in his statement. “There was nobody kinder, more thoughtful, more loyal or more engaging than him. And when it came to laughter, Tom’s was frequent and unmistakable. He is easily summed up by this classic old song: ‘He’s got sunshine on a cloudy day.’”

Added ESPN chairman Jimmy Pitaro, “He brought the credibility of an All-Pro NFL player, the insight of a gifted analyst and a warmth and authenticity that connected with generations of football fans.”

ESPN’s NFL studio is named the Chris Berman-Tom Jackson Studio.

Born in Cleveland on April 4, 1951, Thomas Louie Jackson attended John Adams High School in the city before he was recruited by University of Louisville head coach Lee Corso — another future ESPN commentator — to join the Cardinals.

A fourth-round pick (88th overall) by the Broncos in the 1973 NFL Draft, he played in 191 regular-season games, the most in team history when he retired in 1986, and 10 playoff games, all with Denver.

He was a first-team All-Pro in 1977 and 1978 and a three-time Pro Bowl selection and inducted into the team’s Ring of Fame in 1992.

When he retired at 36, Jackson was the NFL’s oldest linebacker.

“An inspirational leader and fierce competitor, TJ was a proud member of the Broncos’ first Super Bowl team [in 1977] that helped establish a winning tradition in Denver,” the team said in a statement. “Off the field, Tom carried himself with class, warmth and humility, forging deep connections and lifelong friendships with teammates and throughout Broncos Country.”

Jackson’s broadcast career began as a co-host of a Broncos Beat weekly program on KCNC-TV in Denver and postgame show on KUSA-TV. He also hosted a daily Behind the Line syndicated sports commentary radio show and was hired by ESPN in 1987.

He received a Sports Emmy in 2009 and awarded the prestigious Pete Rozelle Radio-Television Award by the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 2015. He retired from broadcasting a year later but reunited with Berman for a digital-only edition of NFL Primetime in 2019.

Jackson often said that he had been “blessed to work for two companies in my life: the Denver Broncos and ESPN.”

Survivors include his wife, Jennifer, and his daughters, Taylor and Morgan. Another daughter, Andrea, died in 1997 at age 9 of injuries suffered in a car accident.

Buildings across the United States are celebrating Voyager 1's major milestone.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The Empire State Building glowed in glittering gold last night (Nov. 17) to celebrate NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft hitting one light-day from Earth. And it isn't the only building celebrating this achievement with a sparkling display.

Today (Nov. 18) at 5:16 a.m. EST (1016 GMT), NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft hit one light-day from Earth. About 16 billion miles (about 26 billion kilometers) away, this is the point at which it takes a full day (or 24 hours) for one light particle to get from us to the probe. So any signal we send to Voyager 1 or it sends back now takes a full day as the spacecraft continues to explore interstellar space.

To celebrate the major milestone for the farthest human-made object in history, the Empire State Building in New York City lit up in gold. This golden glow references the Golden Record onboard both the Voyager 1 and 2 spacecraft.

And the Empire State Building wasn't the only major landmark to celebrate the occasion. The Space Needle in Seattle, Washington, and both the Willis Tower and the Skydeck Chicago in Chicago, Illinois have all been illuminated gold to mark the milestone.

The Golden Record that these gold glowing buildings are referencing serves as an inanimate ambassador for Earth, carrying information about humanity, our planet, the other species who live here, the languages we speak, the music we listen to and so much more. It even includes instructions for building a record player to play the record.

The Voyager mission has, and continues to, make incredible scientific discoveries and observations throughout our solar system and now in interstellar space. But this Golden Record provides an additional aspect to the mission that connects us here on Earth to whatever unknown life may exist out there.

If some sort of life forms out in the cosmos were to ever come across Voyager and its Golden Record at any point in the distant future, they might learn a little bit about our small blue dot.

Chelsea Gohd served as a Senior Writer for Space.com from 2018 to 2022 before returning in 2026, covering everything from climate change to planetary science and human spaceflight in both articles and on-camera in videos. With a M.S. in Biology, Chelsea has written and worked for institutions including NASA JPL, the American Museum of Natural History, Scientific American, Discover Magazine Blog, Astronomy Magazine, and Live Science. When not writing, editing or filming something space-y, Gohd is writing music and performing as Foxanne, even launching a song to space in 2021 with Inspiration4. You can follow her online @chelsea.gohd and @foxanne.music

#751. Molly Meldrum, Australian Music Broadcaster and ‘Countdown’ Host, Dies at 83

"Affectionately dubbed 'The Guru,' Molly was the heartbeat, the champion and the spirit of Australian music," his family said in a statement.

Ian “Molly” Meldrum, the Australian broadcaster, journalist and record producer whose weekly television show made stars of international and local acts alike, died Monday (Nov. 23) at Epworth Hospital in Richmond, Melbourne. He was 83. Explore ABBA Elton John Kylie Minogue See latest videos, charts and news

His family said he died peacefully after a long period of ill health. “Affectionately dubbed ‘The Guru,’ Molly was the heartbeat, the champion and the spirit of Australian music,” they said in a statement. “He shaped not only the sound of a nation but also the dreams of generations who grew up with his voice guiding them.” He is survived by his long-term partner, Yan Wongngam. Related Fans Choose LISA's 'Leave With Me' as This Week's Favorite New Music ATEEZ Earn Fourth No. 1 on Billboard 200 With 'GOLDEN HOUR : Part.6' Selena Gomez Helps Couple With Baby's Sex Reveal at Spurs Game, 'With No Hesitation'

From 1974 to 1987, Meldrum presented Countdown, the ABC’s Sunday-evening music program, which he co-created with executive producer Michael Shrimpton and producer-director Robbie Weekes. Across 563 episodes, it became appointment viewing for young Australians, and — years before MTV — a showcase that leaned heavily on music video.

The Australian Recording Industry Association said Monday that Meldrum had spent six decades convincing a country raised on British and American records that its own artists could stand alongside the greats.

That reach extended well beyond Australia. ABBA broke there on the strength of clips Meldrum played after their 1974 Eurovision win, scoring six No. 1 singles within two years, with “Fernando” spending 14 weeks atop the chart. “Molly started playing our videos down in Australia and it seemed as though the rest of the world just woke up,” Björn Ulvaeus later said. Madonna landed her first hit single anywhere in April 1984, when “Holiday” aired on the show. Blondie, Cyndi Lauper, Meat Loaf, John Mellencamp and Boz Scaggs all found early Australian audiences the same way.

At home, his endorsement moved records. When Meldrum told viewers to “do yourself a favour” on a Sunday night, ARIA said record stores braced for a hectic Monday. Countdown turned Skyhooks and Sherbet into national names and gave early platforms to AC/DC, INXS, Olivia Newton-John, Divinyls, Icehouse and a teenage Kylie Minogue. Elton John, a longtime friend, has called Meldrum the best thing that ever happened to Australian music.

Meldrum came to television from print and from the studio. He was writing for the pop weekly Go-Set by 1966 and produced his first No. 1 record in 1969, Russell Morris‘ “The Real Thing.” He went on to cut top 10 hits for Ronnie Burns, Colleen Hewett, Supernaut and the Ferrets, and founded Melodian Records in 1988.

His on-air persona — a cowboy hat, a stammering delivery, an unmistakable enthusiasm — became national shorthand. One of its defining moments came in 1977, when a flustered Meldrum told the then-Prince of Wales he had seen “your mum” in an open carriage in London.

After Countdown ended, Meldrum presented a music segment on the variety show Hey Hey It’s Saturday until 1999. He was made a Member of the Order of Australia in 1986, received ARIA’s Special Achievement Award in 1993, entered the Logie Awards Hall of Fame in 2012 and was inducted into the ARIA Hall of Fame alongside Countdown in 2014 — the first inductees who were not recording artists.

He survived a near-fatal fall from a ladder at his Melbourne home in 2011 that left him in intensive care, and his health declined in later years.

ARIA chief executive Annabelle Herd led the industry tributes. “All of us at ARIA are heartbroken,” she said. “It is impossible to imagine what Australian music would look like without Molly’s long and storied career. He shaped the music taste of a generation of Australians and gave so much of himself for the good of Australian artists, for which our whole industry is eternally grateful.”

Herd noted that Meldrum had used his Hall of Fame induction speech to urge viewers to get behind Australian acts. “It is up to all of us to keep fighting the good fight in his honour,” she said. “Our thoughts are with Molly’s family and loved ones, and with every artist who got their start because he believed in them.”

Singer Kate Ceberano was among the first artists to post. “They don’t make em like that anymore,” she wrote. “My heart is aching today at the loss.”

#750. After 114 Years, the Beverly Hills Hotel Gets a (Night)life

The landmark’s biggest expansion yet adds a supper club, a cocktail bar and, at long last… a screening room.

Wearing a hard hat and a tailored suit, Beverly Hills Hotel general manager John Scanlon surveys the most significant expansion in the iconic Pink Palace’s 114-year history. Amid the BRRRAAAP! of drills and SKREEEE! of scraping metal, he outlines a slate of new amenities, a decade in the making, including a supper club, a screening room and a cocktail bar.

“I’m going to bed at night dreaming about this and waking up thinking about it,” says Scanlon, a Dorchester Collection veteran who previously ran London’s 45 Park Lane. “It’s the first thought that comes into my head in the morning: ‘Where are we at? What have we got to do today?’ ” Related Stories Lifestyle How Raising Cane's Became an A-List Magnet Lifestyle Kristin Chenoweth to Honor Late Dolly Parton With Gay Men's Chorus of Los Angeles at Holiday Shows

Right now, in the lead-up to their simultaneous debut in the coming weeks, the answer is: a lot. Finalize the menus. Hire more staff. Approve the live acts. Close out permits. Eyeball every aesthetic detail. On a terrace, among the property’s paddle-shaped banana leaf plants, Scanlon says in his Irish brogue, with traces of exhilaration and exhaustion, “I’m obsessed.”

Later, over a lunch of McCarthy salads at the Polo Lounge, alongside the hotel’s new food-and-beverage head Megan Doherty, Scanlon explains that this is all an attempt to better serve guests, especially locals. A consultant — in his accounting, a “social anthropologist” — asked regulars what they wanted as the hotel considered renovations to a sizable swath of neglected, interconnected square footage, on the lobby level to the left of the red carpeted entrance, ranging from an unpopular bedroom suite to a ’90s-era business center that “nobody was using anymore.”

Foremost, it turned out, was a desire for a real nightlife option for party-hardly Beverly Hills. The solution is The Supper Club: a 94-seat, high-glam ovular room with skyline views of Century City that aims for neo-retro, akin to Delilah in West Hollywood. Open until 1 a.m., it will feature a no-photos policy, throwback palm tree motifs, coastal Italian dishes from chef Mattia Agazzi (previously of Gucci Osteria) and a sequence of live evening performances, including five-piece bands, which are curated by music director Alex Le Roux, an in-demand industry booker for events like the wedding of Brooklyn Beckham and Nicola Peltz. “This concept perfectly fits into the heritage of this hotel, but allows us to do something fresh,” says Doherty, who previously ran operations for star L.A. chef Evan Funke.

The research also produced a 14-seat screening room, which is tricked out for sound to handle record-release listening events. Its design by Ken Fulk (clients include Pharrell Williams and Gigi Hadid) is inspired by the Holmby Hills screening room of , Louis B. Mayer’s daughter and Hollywood’s preeminent hostess, where she showed films to friends before release.

For his part, Scanlon seems perhaps most enthused about a new, yet-unnamed cocktail bar — “very intimate, very elegant” — which he promises will rival the Dorchester’s offerings, as well as a lobby-oriented lounge, boasting a wraparound veranda, which will present afternoon tea service: “We’ll have bespoke teas and hand-painted china from Royal Crown Derby and custom sterling silver tea stands that have been made by Arthur Price. It’s a Claridge’s-level experience.”

A key challenge for the new spaces is competing with the landmark existing ones, chiefly the Polo Lounge, the Fountain Coffee Room and the Cabana Café. “Our guests know and love and really connect with them, and there’s this nostalgia there,” Scanlon explains. “They are tractor beams. So, with what we’re doing now, it’s been about, ‘What can we do that’s distinctive?’ They need to shine on their own.” He adds, looking up from his McCarthy salad, “a lot of places take the most popular dish off the menu. That’s crazy to me. Make another popular dish!”

#749. What have the talks with Russia and the US in Abu Dhabi achieved for Ukraine?

The first trilateral talks between Ukraine, the US and Russia in nine months have ended with an agreement on exchanging prisoners. Does this mark a genuine breakthrough and a step toward peace?

The two-day talks between delegations from Ukraine, the US and Russia in Abu Dhabi on November 10 and 11 ended without a ceasefire agreement.

The main outcome was an agreement on a prisoner exchange.

"We have agreed on the largest humanitarian release of prisoners, and tomorrow we will finalize the numbers," Jared Kushner announced after the talks. US envoys Kushner and Steve Witkoff arrived in Moscow on Thursday, where they are due to meet President Vladimir Putin.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy had earlier suggested an exchange of "1,000 for 1,000" prisoners, or "1,500 for 1,500." Russia said a large-scale prisoner exchange with Ukraine could take place within the next two to three weeks.

Following the meetings, Zelenskyy wrote on Telegram that the parties had discussed security guarantees and that "the first step should be ending this war and ensuring Ukraine's security." He also stressed that Europe should be involved "at every stage of genuine diplomacy."

Experts interviewed by DW agree that the main outcome of the talks is humanitarian.

"The agreement on a prisoner exchange is already a major step forward," says Artjom Bronzhukov of the Ukrainian think tank Polityka.

Pavlo Lakiychuk of the Ukrainian Center for Global Studies Strategy XXI also viewed it as a "very tangible result." He told DW that "getting our people back is already a major success. That is why it is worth continuing."

A real breakthrough, he added, would be the release of civilian detainees from territories occupied since 2014, particularly people from Crimea, who have been held in Russian prisons for years.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Davyd Arakhamia, head of the ruling Servant of the People parliamentary faction and Ukraine's representative at the talks in Abu Dhabi, gave a positive assessment of the trilateral talks with the US and Russia, expressing hope that an agreement could be reached by the end of the year.

"I think the Russians came with extremely strict instructions, and it was difficult to ease the tone of the discussion. But the way the US representatives structured the talks with a view to the postwar situation in both countries opened up a dialogue, in my opinion, and allowed us to work together more productively," Arakhamia said at a joint press conference with US and Ukrainian representatives following the talks.

Iuliia Osmolovska of the Kyiv office of the international think tank GLOBSEC cautions against reading too much into the positive assessments of the talks from Washington and Kyiv.

"Diplomats taking part in negotiations will never say that everything went badly and that they have no expectations. Even when no results are achieved, they will still emphasize that the talks were constructive," she said. "For anyone familiar with diplomatic language, these are simply standard phrases."

Osmolovska points to a joint assessment by 71 Ukrainian security and defense experts published by GLOBSEC in the summer. According to the assessment, the chances of a peace agreement or at least a ceasefire being reached this year or next stand at just 19%.

She blames this on the fact that neither side is "ready" for genuine negotiations. Russia, in particular, has yet to accept that its objectives cannot be achieved by military means. "What we are seeing now is more of a farce, an attempt by all sides to put a brave face on things and create the impression that something is moving forward," Osmolovska said.

Artjom Bronzhukov sees the talks as a way for Moscow to buy time.

"The visits by the Russian delegation, particularly under the leadership of Vladimir Medinsky, are nothing more than an attempt to stall and sell empty promises to the US administration in the form of grand agreements, in order to continue receiving so-called gestures of goodwill from Washington, such as the lifting of sanctions on Russian diesel," the political scientist says.

Ahead of the talks, several Western media outlets reported on new US proposals concerning disputed territories. The Economist, for example, reported on a proposal to redraw the administrative boundaries of the Donetsk and Luhansk regions. However, a member of the Ukrainian delegation stressed that there had "never been any discussion of concessions on territories occupied by Russia."

Washington made no official comment on the reports.

Kyrylo Budanov, a member of the negotiating delegation and head of the Ukrainian president's office, declined to say whether Russia had used the talks to demand that Ukrainian troops withdraw from the Donbas. Asked by journalists whether Moscow was still insisting that Ukraine pull out of the region, Budanov said the content of the negotiations would remain confidential until an agreement was reached.

"The issues discussed in the talks are matters for negotiation. The only thing that matters is the outcome. Once we achieve it, it will be made public," Budanov said.

The head of the Russian delegation, Vladimir Medinsky, took a different tone, declaring that "every inch of our land will be returned to Russia one way or another." He was responding to reports in European media that Ukraine was rejecting territorial concessions.

In addition to the Crimean Peninsula, annexed in 2014, Russian President Vladimir Putin claims the four Ukrainian regions of Donetsk, Luhansk, Zaporizhzhia and Kherson in their entirety as Russian territory, even though Russia does not have full military control over them.

"Putin is not fighting over villages and ruined cowsheds in the Donbas. He is fighting for geopolitical influence and trying to exploit the collapse of the old world order," says Artjom Bronzhukov.

The expert from the Polityka think tank recalls that Ukraine was already asked in early 2026 to withdraw its troops from the part of the Donbas it controls and turn the area into a free economic zone. Such a zone "would very quickly become a Russian-controlled area," he warns.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Pavlo Lakiychuk questions the idea of changing administrative boundaries.

"Why would Putin stop there?" asks the expert from the Strategy XXI center. In his view, US negotiators are seeking to extract unilateral concessions from Ukraine "step by step" without demanding anything in return from Russia.

Iuliia Osmolovska describes the proposal as "very original," but says it would pose risks for Ukraine's leadership. Even if the Ukrainian delegation agreed to it, which Osmolovska doubts, the decision would have to be explained to the public, which, she says, is not ready to accept it.

The GLOBSEC expert points out that, following the last harsh winter, marked by shortages of electricity and heating, only 5% of Ukrainians were willing to make concessions to Russia in exchange for an end to attacks on the energy sector.

Following the meeting between Jared Kushner, US special envoy Steve Witkoff and Vladimir Putin in Moscow, Volodymyr Zelenskyy said he wants to "coordinate positions with the Americans once again." No further trilateral meetings have been announced so far.

Iuliia Osmolovska believes the parties will sooner or later have to admit that the negotiations have reached a dead end. She expects each side to return to military action.

Pavlo Lakiychuk, by contrast, believes the talks should continue, if only to secure the return of prisoners. He is also convinced that Europeans "will always be there," because the issue is not just the Russian-Ukrainian war but the security of the entire continent.

#748. Inside Stockholm’s Gasometer, Europe’s Most Ambitious New Music Venue: ‘This Will Create Waves Far Beyond Here’

The venue will host its opening performances in March 2027.

On a frigid November morning, Juliene Planté, head of music at Miramis, and the team lead a preview tour of Gasometer, a new venue in Stockholm that’s slated to open in March 2027. Sections of the site are finished, while in others, we sidle between boxes and pallets of wood, and peer over red tape while the site undergoes its legal assessments.

Inside the venue, the scale of the venture becomes clear; our guide says that she’s starstruck every day when she comes into the space. We enter by the rear stage door, facing the pristine, pillarless seated auditorium. It’s easy to see why she feels that way. Related Chris Brown Agrees to Increase Child Support -- For Now -- to Ex Diamond in Bitter Custody Fight Bill Donahue

“Gasometer is not just for Stockholm, or Sweden or the Nordic countries, but for the whole of Europe,” says Planté.

The space features two venues: a main auditorium and a second, more intimate venue built into the Gasometer’s roof meant primarily for intimate gatherings,banquets and dinners. Miramis estimates that the investment into the project so far has totaled €100 million ($109 million).

The venue’s first main space, called Theatre, features three levels of stalls seating and a standing area which is customizable depending on the production. In a theatre format, the room accommodates 1,750 guests and up to 2,300 with floor standing.

Planté speaks proudly of the significance of this venture, which was undertaken by Miramis, the entertainment and hospitality group that already operates the city’s popular Cirkus venue in the Djurgårdsslätten district. Miramis is a sister company to Pophouse Entertainment, a private entertainment company, co-founded by ABBA’s Björn Ulvaeus, which launched the wildly successful ABBA Voyage show in London.

Gasometer will arrive at a time when some of the world’s leading acts are emerging from a variety of countries in Europe, such as RAYE (U.K.), Rosalía (Spain) and Zara Larsson (Sweden). The venue aims to be a standard bearer for creative innovation in the European venue scene, combining the programming diversity of London’s Southbank Centre with the technological advances of Manchester’s Co-op Live and Aviva Studios.

The venue is an ambitious and dazzling undertaking. It repurposes one of two former gasworks in the city’s northern district, and is part of a wider development of the area bringing living and work spaces to Stockholm in an area that was first built in 1899 to supply the city’s growing need for energy, and was eventually decommissioned a century later in 2011.

For the first five years after opening, Gasometer will be home to the Royal Swedish Opera as the city’s opera house is renovated. That has pushed the building’s developers. A specialist stage floor is required to allow the correct level of bounce for ballet performances, and its sound design has been customized to allow for surround sound, with operators enlisting French audio giant L-Acoustics to shape the venue’s sonic profile.

The building’s original features have been meticulously reproduced or preserved, including the brickwork that surrounds the internal venue. An exact replica of its original roof, which was first designed in 1899, features a latticework of wood and steel and reaches 17 meters above the ground.

The Dome is similarly ambitious. Miramis’ focus on hospitality led them to find a way to integrate gastronomy into the building’s plan. The top floor will house a kitchen  that will serve up to 250 people in a restaurant setting and up to 1,000 guests depending on the formation. Swedish chef Stefan Eriksson will shape Gasometer’s gastronomy profile and offerings using local produce. The customizable space can be booked for artist performances, and The Dome and Theatre can run performances concurrently. The group’s garbage room is just 15 square feet, a deliberate decision to ensure the venue operates as efficiently and with as little waste as possible.

It’s easy to see why Planté — formerly executive producer and head of cultural & special events at London’s KOKO — was attracted to the role. The long-term vision and license allows him to plan “5 to 10 years in the future which is a fantastic, unique opportunity.” He says that the independence, away from big groups such as Live Nation or AEGis  “a golden opportunity”  and “so exciting as a programmer, as a producer, to have that creative freedom.”

The venue’s opening season will kick off on March 17 with ALEPH, a production created by composer Jacob Mühlrad and artist and creative director Alexander Wessely, whose work includes staging for The Weeknd and Rihanna. Across the opening weekend, FKA twigs, Patti Smith and performance artist Marina Abramović, as well as a special score composed and arranged by Mühlrad, and the choreography of Sir Wayne McGregor of the U.K.’s Royal Ballet will perform.

“I want people to feel small when they step into the gasholder, as they would in a church,” Wessely says of the launch production “In ALEPH, music, choreography, light and sculpture surround the audience from every direction. Bringing these artists together in a single work makes it a ritual rather than a traditional concert.”

In Planté’s mind, Gasometer’s programming and building is incomparable to anywhere else in the world. “This is not simply a venue opening. It is a statement of what live performance can become,” he proudly says. For the venue’s first five years, the show will run annually, with new acts expected to perform each time. Alongside the Royal Swedish Opera’s regular performances, Planté will be in charge of 10 nights of programming a year, alongside an additional 10 nights of co-production with the Opera. “For each of those nights, I really want to make them count. I want to programme historic moments,” he says.

He intends to ensure all fans who walk through the venue’s doors remember the performance they witnessed for a long time to come. “I would love to develop a unique format to invite artists to perform with the backing of an orchestra, which is often their goal.” He points to performances by Portishead, Little Simz and Loyle Carner, where having a backing orchestra served to elevate their work.  He says he considers Nick Cave as a dream booking, and he hopes some day artists will release live performances of their albums recorded at Gasometer. While the venue will not be a standard stop for touring artists,  it will be a place for those who want to push their creativity and try something new.

It adds up to a bold new frontier for Europe’s music scene. Come March, Plante says he knows that the Gasometer’s impact will be impossible to ignore: “This will have some waves far beyond here, for sure.”

#747. Net zero emissions won’t reverse climate change — some nations look to ‘net negative’

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

A display reminds those attending the COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, of their goal: limiting global warming to 1.5 ºC.Credit: Metin Aktas/Anadolu/Getty

Net zero is no longer enough. Among countries at the COP31 climate summit under way in Antalya, Turkey, there’s a growing recognition that meeting climate targets will require the world to go ‘net negative’, which means removal of more carbon dioxide from the air than is added.

Scientists say that climate ‘overshoot’ — exceeding 1.5 °C of warming, a target set in 2015 in the landmark Paris agreement — is now inevitable in the next few years. Reaching net-zero status would halt the rise in temperatures. But only achieving net-negative status can bring temperatures back below the 1.5 °C threshold this century.

Can AI actually help the climate? Nations want to harness the technology to cut emissions

Can AI actually help the climate? Nations want to harness the technology to cut emissions

That reality has made net negative and the enormous amount of CO2 removal that would be needed to achieve it a prominent idea at the summit. A coalition of eight countries called the Group of Negative Emitters (GONE) has been working to convince other nations to adopt net-negative targets and get serious about CO2 removal. The group announced that it will be co-chaired by Denmark and Ethiopia, which is hosting next year’s climate summit and could put net negative at the top of the agenda.

“We are in an era of overshoot, and we have to do a lot in terms of removing carbon dioxide,” Ethiopian ambassador Samuel Addis Alemayehu said at a GONE event on 18 November, touting the nation’s progress on reforestation.

Some climate campaigners worry that CO2 removal technologies won’t work and that focusing on them could distract countries from cutting emissions. Despite those concerns, the latest draft of the main statement from COP31 recognizes that CO2 removal has a role in addressing the overshoot, and welcomes efforts to “urgently and rapidly” scale up development of removal methods.

According to a United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) report1 released ahead of the meeting, the world can expect about 1.8 °C of warming this century, even in the most optimistic emissions scenario.

Every fraction of a degree above 1.5 °C raises the risk of climate disasters such as wildfires and powerful hurricanes. “COP31 will be judged a failure if we don’t address the overshoot,” said Ilana Seid, Palau’s ambassador to the UN and chair of the Association of Small Island States, at a press briefing held during the summit.

Many countries at the meeting have discussed slashing emissions to limit the size and duration of the coming overshoot. Turkey has pushed to implement a target of 35% of global energy demand being met with electricity by 2035, a proposal that has gained support from more than 75 countries at the conference and is also included in the draft statement.

But the UNEP report estimates that to recover from overshoot, at least 330 billion tonnes of CO2 would have to be pulled out of the atmosphere this century after the world reaches net zero. Removing that much CO2 would require a vast expansion of existing efforts. Today, about two billion tonnes of CO2 per year are removed by nature-based projects such as reforestation, which takes advantage of the carbon absorbed by growing trees. Scaling up carbon removal quickly enough to achieve net negative and storing carbon in a more durable form will require technological CO2 removal solutions as well.

"3 Body Problem," Netflix's unsettling adaptation of the first book in Chinese author Cixin Liu's epic alien invasion trilogy, "Remembrance of Earth’s Past," made a serious impact on viewers searching for hardcore E.T. drama and now an explosive new trailer for season 2 has just entered our orbit.

This sensational saga about a malevolent interstellar society trying to exist within the unpredictable orbital mechanics of a planet and its triple sun system that forms an Earth-bound armada still has us a bit slack-jawed more than two years after debuting in 2024. Now we're admittedly eager for this shortened 6-episode sophomore outing, which is officially arriving on Jan. 14, 2027.

Delivered by Emmy Award-winning "Game of Thrones" team of David Benioff and D.B. Weiss and "True Blood's" Alexander Woo, "3 Body Problem" season 2 revolves around the combined forces of the Planetary Defense Council as they mount a daring deep space counterattack against the San-Ti.

These Trisolarians are not the friendliest of galactic neighbors, and prior to the all-out invasion their primary goal was to thwart humanity’s ability to create advanced defense weaponry in the four centuries it would take for them to enter our solar system. This time it's more about the next phase of ultimate survival and dire actions taken by anti-alien and pro-alien factions.

Season 2 leaps forward 400 years and focuses on the results of the Wallfacer Project, a secret initiative where chosen individuals worked on solutions in isolation as to not attract the attention of the Trisolarian's omnipresent AI surveillance technology called sophons.

While the debut season was based on Liu's Hugo Award-winning 2008 novel, "The Three-Body Problem," this upcoming Netflix offering will adapt the second book, "The Dark Forest." 2010's "Death's End" closed out the acclaimed sci-fi trilogy.

"So much of season 1 is about the mystery of what's happening," co-creator and co-executive producer David Benioff tells Netflix. "By the time season 2 starts, we have a lot more information. We know there is a hostile alien civilization out there, the San-Ti, and they’re coming our way, and they want our planet for themselves."

Landing on Jan. 14, 2027, "3 Body Problem" season 2's international cast includes returners Jess Hong, Benedict Wong, Jovan Adepo, Eiza González, Liam Cunningham, Marlo Kelly, Sea Shimooka, Saamer Usmani, Alex Sharp and Josh Brener. Joining them are fresh cast members Claudia Doumit, Ellie de Lange, Alfie Allen, David Yip and Jordan Sunshine.

#745. The Hotel Bel-Air’s Menu Returns to Tradition

Everything old is new again, as classic hits are revived, from the Thai-style chicken salad to the house burger.

Since Wolfgang Puck’s 2023 departure from the Hotel Bel-Air and its eponymous restaurant, the luxury lodging has been tweaking its Cal-Med menus with classical French techniques and hyper-seasonal ingredients. The approach was ambitious, evolving, at times even experimental. Yet the largely local dining clientele — 70 percent of weekly regulars are neighbors — who treat the place as a second home (or maybe a fourth, given their net worth) have made it clear they prefer familiarity over ingenuity. Under new executive chef Ralf Schlegel (far left), previously of The Peninsula in Beverly Hills, the kitchen has turned back toward the classics.

The bill of fare has long had a dedicated section of “Bel-Air Classics”: the tortilla soup, the club sandwich, the chopped salad named for late No. 1 fan Nancy Reagan. Now, the restaurant has restored several other salads that had been relegated to off-menu, only-by-request status — Thai-style chicken, soy ginger BBQ salmon, burrata with squash — along with the house burger.

“When you go home, you want what you remember,” explains Hotel Bel-Air manager Tiffany Lai, who insists the restaurant’s back-to-basics pivot won’t condemn it to culinary ossification. “We’re still busy creating new favorites.” She points to the German-born, Austria-raised Schlegel’s signature dish: chicken schnitzel with lemon paprika (left). “Maybe in 15 years that’ll be the next classic.”

#744. Can the EU make it harder to trick consumers online?

The EU wants to curb subscription traps, misleading sales tactics and features that keep people scrolling. What would the proposed Digital Fairness Act change, and does it go far enough?

You sign up for a free trial to watch a series after work. A month later, you've forgotten about it. Then you find a charge for your new 12-month subscription on your bank statement. Sound familiar? You're not alone. Now the EU wants to stop that practice.

Under the European Commission's proposed Digital Fairness Act (DFA), a company would have to remind you before the free trial ends and get your explicit agreement before it can start charging you. The proposed law would also make it easier to cancel a subscription online and require reminders before certain contracts renew automatically.

The Commission presented the proposal on Wednesday. It wants to give consumers more control over how much time and money they spend online.

"We haven't seen that kind of reform in consumer protection in the last 20 years," Agustin Reyna, director general of the European Consumer Organisation (BEUC), told DW.

His organization pushed for stronger EU rules against manipulative online practices. He sees the proposal as a good starting point for tackling problems that frustrate consumers every day.

The proposal also includes a ban on manipulative marketing tactics, so-called "dark patterns." A concrete example: You are trying to reserve a hotel room and the website claims that only three are left, a potentially false claim to pressure you into buying.

A concert ticket that gets more expensive while you're waiting in an online queue raises a different problem. The price could still go up in the process, but the seller would have to show the current price while you wait and tell you the maximum you could be asked to pay.

Online games that encourage users to spend their money to advance are also targeted. Children would no longer be able to pay to win or get to the next level of their online game.

Marketing and personalized ads would need to be clearly marked and restricted in the case of children. Consumers should get the option to switch off doomscrolling functions such as the autoplay of videos, showing one clip after the other. With these new rules, the EU wants to make apps and websites less addictive.

For Christoph Busch, an academic with a focus on consumer law and digital services based at Osnabrück University in Germany, the option to opt out doesn't go far enough. He argues that a version in which consumers actively have to choose to opt into those functions would be more effective.

"But then there is always the question of proportionality," Busch said. "And I think here the European legislators are trying to balance different interests."

These competing interests are particularly visible in the gaming industry, where interest groups have warned that the proposed EU restrictions could hurt developers and leave players with fewer options to choose from.

Video Games Europe and the European Games Developer Federation called the proposal "unworkable, unjustified and disproportionate," arguing that a ban on selling children features that help them win or advance is worded so broadly that it "could cover almost any purchase in a game."

For Busch, this argument doesn't hold. "If your business model is based on addictive design features, then maybe your business model has to be reviewed," he said.

Catalina Goanta, an associate professor of private law and technology at Utrecht University, emphasized in an interview with DW that "regulation can very easily slide into overregulation."

Even though she believes that the DFA is a solid and reasonable compromise, she argues that prohibiting dark patterns and doomscrolling altogether would be too prohibitive. Many of the issues consumers currently face could be resolved by enforcing existing regulation more effectively, she said.

She points to the fact that the EU has made a name for itself in the past by adding new rules and regulations that have made it more difficult to access the European market, especially for small online businesses.

"Instead of having 27 different regulations to adhere to, companies will now only get one," Reyna said.

For him, this speaks for simplification, especially when the responsibility for compliance is shared between online influencers and the platforms they publish on.

According to the new legislation, the EU would have the possibility to impose fines of up to six percent of a company's global annual revenue should the company violate the law.

The European Parliament and the Council, which represents member state governments, still have to agree on the text and formally adopt it. All experts agree that in that process, changes are still very likely.

"It will be a difficult trialogue, especially in this climate of simplification and deregulation with a focus on strengthening European competitiveness," said Christoph Busch. In that climate, it is not easy to add consumer rights, he adds.

Agustin Reyna is more optimistic. "The parliament is a divided house, much more than in the past," he says. "But consumer protection is a subject that brings parties together because it brings tangible outcomes to people."

#743. Sheila Mangubat, ’90 Day Fiancé: Before the 90 Days’ Star, Dies at 35

She appeared on season six of the TLC reality series with her former fiancé, David Dangerfield.

Sheila Mangubat, who starred on season six of the TLC reality series 90 Day Fiancé: Before the 90 Days, has died. She was 35.

David Dangerfield, Mangubat’s former fiancé, shared on Instagram that she died on Saturday in the Philippines. Her cause of death wasn’t immediately available.

“It breaks my heart to share the news from her family that Sheila passed away on Saturday in the Philippines,” Dangerfield wrote. “I am devastated and still trying to process this loss. Please keep her son, her family, and me in your prayers. Thank you for all your love and support.” Related Stories TV Tom Jackson, Denver Broncos' All-Pro Linebacker and ESPN Analyst, Dies at 75 Movies Lance Broadway, Pitcher Turned 'Olympus Has Fallen' Actor, Dies at 43

Before the 90 Days, which launched in 2017, is a spinoff of the original TLC series 90 Day Fiancé. It follows Americans who connect with their partner online and travel abroad to meet them in person for the first time, as they decide whether to propose and apply for a K-1 visa. The original show centers on couples who are already engaged and must decide to get married or break up.

Mangubat and Dangerfield’s relationship was documented on Before the 90 Days season six in 2023. After meeting through a Facebook group for deaf and hearing-impaired singles in 2021, Dangerfield traveled from Nebraska to the Philippines to meet his then-girlfriend Mangubat in person for the first time. They eventually got engaged on the show but later broke up in October 2025 due to K-1 visa issues, financial strain and distance.

Mangubat is survived by her son, Jhonreil, from a previous relationship.

The moon shines with Saturn in the constellation Pisces after sunset on Nov. 20

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The moon shines close to the ringed giant Saturn after sunset tonight (Nov. 20), presenting a spectacular naked-eye display as the stars of the Great Square of Pegasus twinkle nearby.

Saturn's steady light will appear a little over 5 degrees from the 82%-lit moon in the southeastern sky after the sun dips below the horizon for viewers in the U.S. — roughly the width of your three middle fingers held at arm's length.

Moonlight will hide fainter stars from view, though you should be able to spot Algenib, Markab, Alpheratz and Scheat arrayed in a diamond formation above the lunar disk, marking out the asterism of the Great Square of Pegasus in the November sky.

The moon will present a spectacular target through the eyepiece of a 6-inch telescope, as the terminator line separating night from day creeps ever closer to its western edge. It's a great time to explore the 110 km-wide Gassendi Crater on the edge of Mare Humorum as its eastern rim and central peaks throw intense shadows across its interior.

Slewing your telescope over to Saturn will reveal details and subtle variations in the cloud surface of the gas giant, along with its iconic ring system, which is gradually becoming more visible following its ring plane crossing in March 2025.

Depending on viewing conditions, you may also notice a shoal of bright, star-like points of light surrounding Saturn's disk, which represent the large moons Titan, Dione, Tethys, Rhea and Iapetus.

Interested in seeing the planets of the solar system up close for yourself? Then be sure to check out our picks of the best telescopes available in 2026, including the Celestron NexStar 8SE, which we rate as the best motorized scope out there.
